definition_zh: 引诱；诱惑；吸引；鼓动；怂恿
definition_en: to make someone want to do something, especially something unwise or wrong, or to attract someone strongly
core_image: 一只手把诱人的东西举到面前，另一只脚正要迈出去
scene: 深夜，橱窗里的巧克力蛋糕还亮着灯。The smell of fresh bread tempted her to break her diet for one evening, but she walked home a little faster.
sceneCN: 这里 tempt 是「引诱、诱惑」（第 1 个义项：让人忍不住想做某件不该做的事）；句意：新鲜面包的香味诱惑她破一次减肥的规矩，她还是加快了脚步回家。

pos.zh: 动词：引诱、诱惑；吸引、使很想做；鼓动、怂恿

collocations.zh: 很想做某事；忍不住想做某事
诱人的提议（由本词加 -ing 构成）
把某人从某处或某事上引开

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「诱惑；诱惑人的事物」
由本词加 -ing 构成形容词，义为「诱人的；令人心动的」
由本词加 -er 构成施动名词，义为「诱惑者」，也指圣经里的试探者
由形容词 tempting 再加 -ness 构成，义为「诱惑性」

senses.title: To lure someone toward something wrong
senses.titleCN: 引诱；诱惑（做不该做的事）
senses.definition: to make someone want to do something that is unwise, wrong, or against their better judgment
senses.definitionCN: 使某人想做不明智、不对或违背自己判断的事
senses.example: The glowing shop window tempted her to spend her last coins.
senses.exampleCN: 亮闪闪的橱窗诱使她花掉了最后的几个硬币。
senses.why: Latin temptare means to try or to test: an offer puts the desire to try on trial, and the tempting thing is the test itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 temptare 意为「尝试、考验」：一个诱人的东西把「想试一试」的念头推到人面前接受考验，诱因本身就是那场考验。

senses.title: To attract and make someone want
senses.definition: to attract someone so strongly that they feel a wish to do or have something, often in the phrase be tempted to
senses.definitionCN: 强烈地吸引某人，使其产生想做或想拥有的愿望，常用于 be tempted to 结构
senses.example: I was tempted to skip the meeting and walk in the park instead.
senses.exampleCN: 我差点忍不住跳过会议，去公园散步。
senses.why: The test no longer needs a moral plot: any bright offer can pull the mind a little, and the phrase be tempted to records that pull.
senses.whyCN: 考验不必再牵涉道德情节：任何亮眼的提议都能把心思轻轻拉一下，be tempted to 记下的就是这一拉。

senses.title: To provoke or dare
senses.definition: to try to persuade or provoke someone into doing something, especially something reckless
senses.definitionCN: 试图说服或激某人去做某事，尤指鲁莽的事
senses.example: The older boys tempted him to climb the rusty water tower.
senses.exampleCN: 大男孩们怂恿他去爬那座生锈的水塔。
senses.why: A test can be set by one person for another: to tempt someone is to put the trial in front of them and watch whether they rise to it.
senses.whyCN: 考验可以由一个人设在另一个人面前：tempt 就是把这场试探摆到对方面前，看对方会不会迎上去。

senses.title: Tempt fate: to risk disaster
senses.definition: in the phrase tempt fate or tempt providence, to act in a risky way that invites bad luck or disaster
senses.definitionCN: 用于 tempt fate 或 tempt providence，指做出招惹厄运或灾难的冒险举动
senses.example: Driving on those bald tyres in the rain is tempting fate.
senses.exampleCN: 雨天还开着磨平了的轮胎，是在玩命。
senses.why: If the world is a tester, then to tempt fate is to dare the tester to try you, and that is exactly what brings trouble.
senses.whyCN: 如果世界就是出题者，那么 tempt fate 就是主动请出题者来考你，而这恰恰招来了麻烦。

senses.title: To attract buyers or attention
senses.definition: to attract customers, investors, or interest by offering something appealing, as in a commercial or public context
senses.definitionCN: 通过提供有吸引力的东西来吸引顾客、投资者或兴趣，多用于商业或公共语境
senses.example: The airline tempted travellers with cheap fares and free luggage.
senses.exampleCN: 这家航空公司用低价机票和免费行李吸引旅客。
senses.why: In trade the test becomes a display: a good offer is the bright object held up in front of a passer-by.
senses.whyCN: 在商业里，考验变成了展示：一个好价钱就是举在路人面前的那件亮眼之物。

senses.title: To be enticed into a trap
senses.definition: to draw someone into a situation or action by means of a lure, often deliberately and to their disadvantage
senses.definitionCN: 用诱饵把某人引入某种处境或行动，往往是有意的且对其中不利
senses.example: The false listing tempted the buyers into paying a deposit.
senses.exampleCN: 那条虚假的房源把买家诱进了交定金的圈套。
senses.why: Once the lure is placed on purpose, the test becomes a snare: the desire to take the offer is the door of the trap.
senses.whyCN: 一旦诱饵是故意放置的，考验就变成了陷阱：想要得到那份好处的欲望，就是陷阱的门。

intro.en: Tempt comes from Latin temptare through Old French, and it first names a test rather than a wish.
intro.cn: tempt 经由古法语来自拉丁语 temptare，它最初指的是一场考验，而不是一种欲望。

items.en: The verb temptare meant to try, to attempt, or to test, and its own deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 动词 temptare 意为「尝试、试做、考验」，它更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Spelling with a p, temptare, and without one, tentare, both appear in Latin; the two forms are usually treated as variants of one verb.
items.cn: 写 p 的 temptare 与不写 p 的 tentare 在拉丁语中都出现，通常被视为同一个动词的不同写法。

items.en: Old French tempter carried the testing sense forward, with a strong pull toward the idea of leading into evil.
items.cn: 古法语 tempter 延续了「考验」的含义，并明显偏向「引人作恶」的意思。

items.en: English records tempt from about the thirteenth century, and early use is heavily shaped by Bible translation, where the devil tempts Christ.
items.cn: 英语自十三世纪前后有 tempt 的记录，早期用法深受圣经翻译影响，其中魔鬼试探基督。

items.en: The moral sense widened into the everyday one: an offer, a price, a smell or a glance can now tempt anyone.
items.cn: 道德义逐渐扩展到日常义：如今一个提议、一个价钱、一股香味或一个眼神都能引诱任何人。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the same Latin testing root and its English family; the near-meaning group gathers enticers that differ in tone and in who is being pulled.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁语「考验」词根及其英语词族；近义组收各类「引」人的词，区别在语气以及被引的对象。

entries.definition: The noun for the desire to do something you know you should not do, or the thing that creates it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「诱惑；诱人之物」，指想做不该做之事的欲望，或引起这种欲望的东西。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning appealing enough to make you want to give in.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「诱人的、令人心动的」，指好到让人想顺从的程度。

entries.definition: Someone who entices another person, and in religious language the one who tempts people to sin.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「诱惑者」，在宗教语境中指引人犯罪者。

entries.definition: To attract someone, often by trickery and usually with a bait or a promise.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「引诱、诱捕」，常带欺骗意味，多以诱饵或许诺引人。

entries.definition: To persuade someone to do something by offering pleasure or advantage; a little more deliberate than tempt.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「引诱、怂恿」，用快乐或好处劝人去做，比 tempt 更有「刻意」的意味。

entries.definition: To persuade someone into doing something wrong or foolish, especially by charm; stronger and more formal.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「引诱、蛊惑」，多指用魅力把人引向错误或愚蠢之事，语气更强也更正式。

normalIntro.en: These hooks work from the real Latin verb temptare, to test, and from the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子基于真实的拉丁语动词 temptare「考验」，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: temptare is to test: the sweet chocolate is set in front of you as a test, and that is tempt.
normal.cn: temptare 是「考验」：香甜的巧克力摆在面前当作考题，这就是 tempt。

normal.en: attempt also comes from the same verb: one tries a task, the other tests a person.
normal.cn: attempt 同出这一动词：一个试的是任务，另一个考的是人。

normal.en: To be tempted to do something means to feel a strong pull toward it.
normal.cn: be tempted to do something 意为被强烈地拉向某件事。

normal.en: Temptation adds -ation to the verb and names the thing or the wish that pulls.
normal.cn: temptation 在动词后加 -ation，指出那个拉着人的诱因或念头。

normal.en: Tempt fate means to dare bad luck on purpose.
normal.cn: tempt fate 意为故意去招惹坏运气。

abstract.en: Picture a hand holding out a bright sweet while another hand reaches for it, half pulling back.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手举着一颗亮晶晶的糖，另一只手伸过去，却又缩回一半。

abstract.en: The knife stays on the table untouched: being tempted is wanting the cut, not making it.
abstract.cn: 刀还静静地放在桌上没被拿起：被诱惑是想去拿，而不是已经拿了。

abstract.en: Think of a shop sign that is too bright, so everyone slows down and looks.
abstract.cn: 想象一块亮得过分的店招，让每个路过的人都慢下来多看一眼。

examples.en: The fresh bread in the bakery window tempted him to buy a second loaf.
examples.cn: 面包店橱窗里的新鲜面包诱使他多买了一条。

examples.en: She was tempted to tell nobody about the mistake.
examples.cn: 她一度很想不告诉任何人这个错误。

examples.en: Low prices tempted many tourists into the small shop.
examples.cn: 低廉的价格把许多游客吸引进了那家小店。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「吞它」——好东西摆在眼前，忍不住想「吞它」，就是被诱惑；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 temptare（尝试、试验、考验）→ 古法语 tempter（引诱、试探）→ 英语 tempt，核心义「把东西摆到面前，看你受不受得住」。拉丁语写作 temptare 与 tentare 两种形式并见，tempt 的 p 保留自前一种写法；temptare 更早的来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses of tempt all turn one idea: a test placed in front of a person, from a moral lure, through a strong pull and an open dare, to an offer, a snare and a dare to fate.
sensesIntro.cn: tempt 的六个义项都在转同一个念头：把一道考验摆在人面前，从道德上的诱因，到强烈的拉扯，再到明晃晃的怂恿、商业上的吸引、设下的圈套，以及对命运的挑衅。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bright thing is held out in front of a person, and the pull of it is the test.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件亮眼的东西被举到人面前，那股拉力就是考验。

branches.en: THE MORAL TEST: the offer is something you know you should refuse, and the sense names that trial.
branches.cn: 道德考验线：这份诱惑是你明知该拒绝的，义项指的就是这场考验。

branches.en: THE PULL: with be tempted to, any small wish becomes a strong tug, without moral weight.
branches.cn: 拉力线：在 be tempted to 里，任何小小的愿望都变成一股强拉，不带道德重量。

branches.en: THE DARE: one person sets the test for another and waits to see whether they rise to it.
branches.cn: 挑衅线：一个人给另一个人出题，等着看对方会不会迎上去。

branches.en: THE DARE TO FATE: the world itself becomes the tester, and the risk is the answer.
branches.cn: 挑命线：世界本身成了出题者，冒险就是给出的答案。

branches.en: THE DISPLAY AND THE SNARE: a commercial offer is the bright object held out, and once it is placed on purpose, it is a trap.
branches.cn: 展示与陷阱线：商业上的优惠就是举出来的亮眼之物，一旦是故意放置的，它就成了一张网。

intro.en: Tempt is a single Latin verb brought forward through French; English builds the family with ordinary suffixes such as -ation, -ing and -er.
intro.cn: tempt 是经由法语传来的一个拉丁语动词；英语用 -ation、-ing、-er 这类普通后缀建起这一词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin temptare and its variant tentare are recorded, and the derived adjective and noun in English are transparent, so only the deeper origin is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 temptare 及其异体 tentare 均有文献记录，英语中的形容词与名词派生也很清楚，只有更早的来源属于重构或存疑。

items.example: The Latin verb supplies the testing image.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁语动词提供「考验」的意象。

items.example: The variant without p shows how the two spellings were used side by side.
items.exampleCN: 不带 p 的异体说明两种写法曾被并用。

items.example: Old French brought the word into English.
items.exampleCN: 古法语把这个词带入英语。

items.example: It forms temptation.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 temptation。

items.meaning: a strong wish to do what is wrong
items.example: Temptation names the pull itself.
items.exampleCN: temptation 指的是那股拉力本身。

items.example: It forms tempting.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 tempting。

items.example: A tempting offer is one hard to refuse.
items.exampleCN: a tempting offer 是让人难以拒绝的提议。

items.example: It forms tempter.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 tempter。

items.example: Attempt keeps the trying sense of the Latin verb.
items.exampleCN: attempt 保留了拉丁语动词「尝试」的一面。

definition_zh: 站得住脚的；可守住的；能维持的；可防守的
definition_en: able to be defended against attack or objection, and so able to hold up as reasonable or true
core_image: 一处阵地被守住了，敌方的冲击推不动它
scene: 会议开到一半，有人对预算提出质疑。After two more rounds of questions, the original proposal was still tenable, so the board approved it.
sceneCN: 这里 tenable 是「站得住脚的」（第 1 个义项：经得起反驳、可以维持的主张）：又经过两轮追问，最初的提案依然站得住脚，董事会便通过了它。

pos.zh: 形容词：站得住脚的；可守住的；能维持的

collocations.zh: 守得住的防御（多用于军事）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「站得住脚性；可守性」
由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「站得住脚地」
由否定前缀 un- 加本词构成，义为「站不住脚的；无法维持的」
同出拉丁语 tenere「握住」，义为「任期；终身教职；保有」

senses.title: Able to be defended as reasonable
senses.definition: capable of being defended against criticism or objection, and therefore reasonable or acceptable to hold
senses.definitionCN: 经得起批评或反驳，因而可以合理地持有或被接受的
senses.example: The evidence was thin, so the claim was no longer tenable.
senses.exampleCN: 证据单薄，这个说法已经站不住脚了。
senses.why: Latin tenere means to hold: an argument you can hold your ground with is one that tenable describes, since it can be held up against every push.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 tenere 意为「握住、守住」：你站得住阵地去说出的论点，正是 tenable 所形容的——它能顶住每一次冲击继续被握住。

senses.title: Able to be held against attack
senses.definition: capable of being held or defended against a military attack
senses.definitionCN: 能抵挡军事进攻、坚守得住的
senses.example: The hill was tenable only if the river crossing was covered.
senses.exampleCN: 只有守住渡口，这座山丘才守得住。
senses.why: The oldest use is military: a position that can still be held when the enemy pushes is tenable, and that is the image the word grew from.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的用法是军事上的：敌方推来时仍守得住的位置就是 tenable，这个词的整体意象正从这幅画面长出。

senses.title: Able to be maintained over time
senses.definition: able to be kept going, supported, or continued without breaking down, especially a system, price, or arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 能够维持、支撑或继续下去而不至于崩溃的，多指制度、价格或安排
senses.example: That rent was tenable for a year, but not for five.
senses.exampleCN: 那样的房租维持一年还行，五年就撑不住了。
senses.why: Holding can be long as well as firm: if a load can be carried for years, the arrangement can be held, and so it is tenable.
senses.whyCN: 「握住」不仅要求稳，也要求久：如果一份负担能被扛上几年，这个安排就握得住，所以它是 tenable。

senses.title: Belonging to the test of tenure
senses.definition: in academic use, related to tenure, a permanent post, or the assessment that grants it, as in a tenure-track job
senses.definitionCN: 学术语境中指与终身教职或其考核相关的，如 tenure-track 职位
senses.example: A tenure-track post gives you seven years to prove you belong.
senses.exampleCN: 终身教职轨道上的职位给你七年时间去证明自己适合留下。
senses.why: Tenure comes straight from Latin tenere: a post you can keep is a thing held, and the academic use of tenable points back to that holding.
senses.whyCN: tenure 直接源于拉丁语 tenere：能留住的职位就是握住的东西，学术场合里的 tenable 正回指这份「握住」。

senses.title: Untenable: impossible to hold
senses.definition: in the negative form untenable, describing a position, belief, or situation that cannot possibly be defended or kept
senses.definitionCN: 在否定式 untenable 中，描述根本守不住、维持不了的立场、信念或处境
senses.example: When the funding was cut, the whole plan became untenable.
senses.exampleCN: 资金被削减后，整个计划就无法维持了。
senses.why: Remove the un- and the holding returns: untenable simply says the position could not be held, and it is where the holding image is most visible.
senses.whyCN: 拿掉 un- 就回到「握住」：untenable 只是说这个立场握不住，而正是在这个词里，「握住」的意象最清楚。

senses.title: A tenable theory: holding up as science
senses.definition: in scientific and scholarly writing, describing a theory or explanation that has not been refuted and can reasonably be maintained against alternatives
senses.definitionCN: 在科学和学术写作中，指尚未被推翻、在同其他解释的竞争中可以合理坚持的理论或解释
senses.example: Once the new data arrived, the simplest explanation remained tenable.
senses.exampleCN: 新数据到手后，最简单的解释依然说得通。
senses.why: A theory is a bridge in argument: it stands as long as it carries the weight of every objection, and a theory that still carries is tenable.
senses.whyCN: 理论是论证里的一座桥：只要还能承受每一次反驳的重量，它就立着，而还能承重的理论就是 tenable。

intro.en: Tenable is built from the French continued form of Latin tenere, to hold, plus the suffix -able, and it was first used of positions that could be defended.
intro.cn: tenable 由拉丁语动词 tenere「握住」在法语中的形式加后缀 -able 构成，最初用来形容守得住的位置。

items.en: *ten- is generally reconstructed as the sense to stretch or to pull tight, and it lies behind many holding and stretching words in the Indo-European family.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 *ten- 表示「拉伸、绷紧」，印欧语系中许多「握持」与「伸长」的词都追溯到它。

items.en: The verb tenere meant to hold, to keep, or to occupy, and it produced tenax, tenacis, which gives English tenacious.
items.cn: 动词 tenere 意为「握住、保有、占据」，它还生出 tenax（属格 tenacis），也就是英语 tenacious 的来源。

items.en: Old French tenir meant to hold, to keep, and to last; its inflected stem ten- came into English words made with -able.
items.cn: 古法语 tenir 意为「握住、保有、持续」；加上 -able 构成英语词时，用的正是它的词干 ten-。

items.en: The Latin adjective tenabilis, capable of being held, exists as the direct mother of the English adjective.
items.cn: 拉丁语形容词 tenabilis 意为「握得住的」，正是这个英语形容词的直接来源。

items.en: English records tenable from the sixteenth century, first of a fortified place or position that could be held against attack.
items.cn: 英语自十六世纪有 tenable 的记录，最初用于说某处防御工事或阵地守得住。

items.en: The military sense spread to arguments and arrangements: any claim that can be held up is now called tenable, and its opposite untenable.
items.cn: 军事义扩展到了论点和安排：如今任何经得起质疑的主张都叫 tenable，反义则是 untenable。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the same Latin holding root and the words English made from it; the near-meaning group gathers claims that do or do not hold up.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁语「握住」词根及其英语造词；近义组收「站得住」或「站不住」的各类说法。

entries.definition: Impossible to defend or maintain; the negative of tenable, built with the prefix un-.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「站不住脚的、无法维持的」，是本词加否定前缀 un- 构成的否定形式。

entries.definition: The quality of holding on firmly and not giving up, from Latin tenax.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「坚持、顽强」，指紧握不放、不轻言放弃的品质，来自拉丁语 tenax。

entries.definition: Holding firmly to a purpose, or gripping and not letting go.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「顽强的、紧握不放的」，出自同一「握住」词根。

entries.definition: Able to be defended with reasons or with force; very close to tenable, with more court and military flavour.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可辩护的、可守住的」，与 tenable 很接近，法庭与军事色彩更浓。

entries.definition: Seeming reasonable or likely to be true; it points to how a claim sounds, not how well it holds.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「似乎有道理的」，看重的是听起来是否合理，而不是撑不撑得住。

entries.definition: Able to work or survive in practice, referring to plans and projects rather than arguments.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可行的」，指计划、方案在现实中行得通，对象不是论点。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the true Latin verb tenere, which yields plenty of English words about holding on.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子围绕真实的拉丁语动词 tenere，它生出了大量与「握住」有关的英语词。

normal.en: tenere is to hold: a tenable claim is one you can still hold on to after the attacks.
normal.cn: tenere 是「握住」：tenable 的主张就是被攻击之后仍然握得住的主张。

normal.en: The same root gives tenacious, tenacity, tenant and tenure: all of them are about holding or keeping.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 tenacious、tenacity、tenant、tenure，这些词都与握住或保有有关。

normal.en: Tenable starts in the army and moves into the courtroom: first a hill you can hold, then a case you can hold.
normal.cn: tenable 从军营走进法庭：先是守得住的山头，后是站得住的官司。

normal.en: The opposite is made with un-: untenable says the grip has failed.
normal.cn: 反义词由 un- 造出：untenable 表示这一握已经失手。

normal.en: A tenable price or lease is one you can carry for the whole period of the agreement.
normal.cn: a tenable price 或 a tenable lease 指在整个合约期内都扛得住的价钱或租约。

abstract.en: Picture a rope bridge over a gorge: the theory is tenable while the planks still carry the weight of every objection.
abstract.cn: 想象峡谷上的一座绳桥：只要木板还撑得住每一次反驳的重量，这套理论就是 tenable。

abstract.en: See a reporter halfway up a ladder of sandbags, still standing when the fifth wave hits.
abstract.cn: 想象一名记者站在沙袋垒成的梯子上，第五波冲击来时还没有倒下。

abstract.en: Think of an old shop that is fine for one winter but too cold to carry through five.
abstract.cn: 试想一家老店，撑一个冬天没问题，可是撑过五个冬天就太冷了。

examples.en: On the current figures, the theory is still tenable.
examples.cn: 以现有数据看，这一理论依然站得住脚。

examples.en: The garrison held the tenable ridge until the relief column arrived.
examples.cn: 守军守住了那道可守的山脊，直到援军到达。

examples.en: Without a second income, the loan was simply not tenable.
examples.cn: 没有第二份收入，这笔贷款根本维持不住。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「特能包」——特别能包住底，怎么问都不垮，当然站得住脚；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 tenere（握住、保有、占据）→ 其形容词 tenabilis（握得住的）→ 古法语词干 ten- + -able → 英语 tenable。同根词：tenacious、tenacity、tenant、tenure、contents（由 continere 构成）。原始印欧语 *ten-「拉伸、绷紧」为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses of tenable all come from one grip: a position held against attack, a claim held against argument, an arrangement held through time, a post held in academia, and the theory or deal that stops holding.
sensesIntro.cn: tenable 的六个义项都来自同一次「握住」：守得住的阵地、顶得住反驳的主张、扛得住时间的安排、学术界里留得住的职位，以及最后握不住的理论或交易。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hilltop position is still held when the fifth wave breaks against it.
core.cn: 核心意象：第五波冲击撞上来，山顶阵地依然被握在手里。

branches.en: THE BATTLEFIELD: the first and most concrete sense, a place that can still be held against attack.
branches.cn: 战场线：最初、也最具体的一个义项，指顶着进攻仍能守住的阵地。

branches.en: THE ARGUMENT: the enemy becomes an objection, and a claim that can still be held is a tenable one.
branches.cn: 论辩线：敌人换成了反驳，顶得住的论点就是 tenable 的论点。

branches.en: THE LONG HAUL: holding a price or a lease is holding it through years, not through one wave.
branches.cn: 长久线：扛住价格或租约意味着一扛就是多年，而不是一波冲击。

branches.en: THE CAMPUS: tenure keeps the holding idea in the academy, where a post is also a thing to be held.
branches.cn: 校园线：tenure 把「握住」带进学界，那里的职位同样是握在手里的东西。

branches.en: THE FAILED GRIP: untenable is the moment the hand lets go, and it shows the image most plainly.
branches.cn: 失手线：untenable 是手松开的那一刻，也正是最能看清这个意象的地方。

intro.en: Tenable is a Latin holding verb plus an English-received suffix -able; the negation un- and the noun suffix -ity complete the set.
intro.cn: tenable 是拉丁语「握住」动词加后缀 -able 构成的形容词，再加否定前缀 un- 与名词后缀 -ity 形成完整一组。

latinIntro.en: Latin tenere, tenax and tenabilis are all documented, so the holding root itself is secure; only the earliest Indo-European layer is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tenere、tenax、tenabilis 均有文献可查，「握住」词根本身可靠，只有最早的印欧语层是重构形式。

items.example: The Latin verb is the holding root.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁语动词是「握住」的词根。

items.example: It is the direct model of the English adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个英语形容词的直接范本。

items.example: It gives English tenacious.
items.exampleCN: 它给出英语的 tenacious。

items.example: It forms tenable from the holding stem.
items.exampleCN: 它把「握住」词干变成 tenable。

items.example: It forms tenability.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 tenability。

items.example: It forms tenably.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 tenably。

items.example: It forms untenable.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 untenable。

items.example: Tenant is literally a holder.
items.exampleCN: tenant 字面上就是「持有者」。

items.meaning: the right to hold a post
items.example: Tenure keeps the same holding idea.
items.exampleCN: tenure 保留了同样的「握住」念头。

definition_zh: 要旨；大意；基调；男高音；次中音声部
definition_en: the general meaning or character of something, or the highest normal adult male singing voice
core_image: 一条持续的嗓音线，从第一个音一路稳稳地拉到结尾
scene: 邮件刚读完，会议室里没有人说话，气氛已经变了。The tenor of the negotiation changed once the raw figures were put on the table.
sceneCN: 这里 tenor 是「基调、要旨」（第 2 个义项：说话、文件或局势的整体意味与走向）；句意：真实的数字一摆上桌，谈判的基调就变了。

pos.zh: 名词：要旨、大意；基调；男高音；次中音声部

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ist 构成，义为「男高音歌手」，与 tenor 同源
字面即「唱高音的另一半」，与 tenor 共享拉丁语「声部」的构词思路，女性最低的声部，可作声部义的对照

senses.title: A continuous course or drift
senses.definition: the general or continuous course that something runs along, especially the drift or tendency of a speech, text, or event
senses.definitionCN: 事物沿着的总体或持续的进程，尤指讲话、文本或事件的走向与倾向
senses.example: Midway through the letter, the tenor of the writer changes.
senses.exampleCN: 信写到一半，作者的走向变了。
senses.why: Latin tenor comes from tenere, to hold, and names a continuous holding-on; the earliest English uses keep that sense of an unbroken course.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 tenor 出自 tenere「握住」，本义是一种不间断的延续；英语最早的用法正保留着「一路不断的进程」这层意思。

senses.title: The general meaning or character
senses.definition: the general meaning, tone or spirit of something said, written or done, taken as a whole rather than word by word
senses.definitionCN: 所说、所写、所为的整体含义、语气或精神，是从总体上把握而非逐字理解的
senses.example: I did not catch every word, but I understood the tenor of the speech.
senses.exampleCN: 我没听清每个字，但听懂了演讲的大意。
senses.why: If meaning is held in a continuous line, its overall direction is the tenor: you may miss single words and still follow the course.
senses.whyCN: 如果意义是被一条连贯的线握着，那么整条线朝向哪里就是 tenor：个别词漏掉，也仍然跟得上这条线。

senses.title: The highest ordinary male voice
senses.definition: the highest normal male singing voice, or the adult male singer who has it
senses.definitionCN: 成年男声中最高的歌喉，或拥有这种歌喉的男歌手
senses.example: The tenor took the last phrase alone, high and clear.
senses.exampleCN: 男高音独自唱了最后一句，又高又清。
senses.why: In medieval music the tenor was the voice that held the sustained melody, the main line; later the word settled on the uppermost male part.
senses.whyCN: 在中世纪音乐里，tenor 是「保持」那条持续旋律的主声部；后来这个词固定指最高的男声声部。

senses.title: A part written in the tenor range
senses.definition: a musical part or instrument set in the range of the tenor voice, such as a tenor saxophone or the tenor part in a choir
senses.definitionCN: 按男高音音域写的声部或乐器，如次中音萨克斯风或合唱中的次中音声部
senses.example: He switched from alto to tenor saxophone last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 他去年春天从高音萨克斯改吹了次中音萨克斯。
senses.why: Once a voice names a range, any part or instrument built for that range borrows the name, and so does the instrument itself.
senses.whyCN: 一旦某个嗓音固定代表一个音域，任何按这个音域写的声部或造出的乐器都会借用这个名字，乐器本身也一样。

senses.title: A settled purpose or intent
senses.definition: the underlying intent or purpose of something, especially in legal writing, where the tenor of a deed is its operative intent
senses.definitionCN: 某事物背后的意图或目的，尤见于法律文本，契约的 tenor 指其实际起作用的意图
senses.example: The tenor of the clause, not its wording, decided the case.
senses.exampleCN: 决定胜负的是这一条款的实际意图，而不是它的字面说法。
senses.why: A document also holds a purpose along its length; the law reads past the words to that held intent and calls it the tenor.
senses.whyCN: 文件也同样沿着自身长度握着一个目的；法律越过了字面去看那个被握住的意图，并把它称作 tenor。

intro.en: Tenor comes from Latin tenor through Old French, and every later sense keeps hold of its source meaning, a continuous holding-on.
intro.cn: tenor 经由古法语来自拉丁语 tenor，此后每个义项都握住它原本的意思：一种不间断的延持。

items.en: The verb tenere meant to hold, to keep, or to continue, and it underlies tenacious, tenant and tenable as well.
items.cn: 动词 tenere 意为「握住、保有、延续」，tenacious、tenant、tenable 都源自它。

items.en: The noun tenor meant a continuous course, a tenor of a tune or a speech, from tenere plus the agent ending -or; it could also name one who holds.
items.cn: 名词 tenor 意为「连续的进程、曲调或言辞的走向」，由 tenere 加施动词尾 -or 构成，它也曾指「持有者」。

items.en: Old French tenor kept both the meaning sense and the musical sense, and it carried the word into English.
items.cn: 古法语 tenor 同时保留了「意义走向」与「音乐声部」两层意思，并把这个词带入英语。

items.en: In medieval polyphony the tenor was the part that held the sustained melody, from Latin tenere, and that is the origin of the singing sense.
items.cn: 在中世纪复调音乐中，tenor 是保持那条持续旋律的声部，源自 tenere，这就是声部义的由来。

items.en: English records tenor from the fourteenth century in the musical sense, with the sense of general meaning well established by the fifteenth.
items.cn: 英语自十四世纪有 tenor 的音乐义记录，「总体意味」这一义项到十五世纪已经确立。

items.en: The word is now used most often for the general tone or character of something, with the musical senses running alongside.
items.cn: 如今这个词最常用来指某事物的总体基调或性质，音乐义则并行保留。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the Latin holding root and English words from it; the near-meaning group gathers words for the sense or tone of what is said.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁语「握住」词根及其英语造词；近义组收描述话语或文字「意思、基调」的各类词。

entries.definition: Able to be defended or maintained, built from the same Latin verb tenere, to hold.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「站得住脚的、可维持的」，由同一拉丁语动词 tenere「握住」构成。

entries.definition: The quality of holding on without giving way, from Latin tenax.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「坚韧、顽强」，指握紧不放的品质，来自拉丁语 tenax。

entries.definition: The right or period of holding a post, literally holding, and the academic post it grants.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「保有、任期、终身教职」，字面即「握住」，并指由此获得的学术职位。

entries.definition: The main point of a speech or text, usually reduced to a few words; less about tone than tenor.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「主旨、要点」，通常浓缩成几句话，比 tenor 更少涉及语调。

entries.definition: The quality or mood of a voice, text or situation, closer to how it sounds than to what it means.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「语调、气氛」，更侧重听起来的样子，而不是意思本身。

entries.definition: The general tendency or direction that something is moving in, often the slow direction of opinion.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「趋势、走向」，指事物运动的总方向，常指舆论的缓慢转向。

normalIntro.en: These hooks work from the real Latin holding root and from the way the word moves from music into meaning.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子基于真实的拉丁语「握住」词根，以及这个词从音乐走向「意义」的路径。

normal.en: tenere is to hold: a tenor line is the melody held from the first note to the last.
normal.cn: tenere 是「握住」：tenor 声部就是从头到尾被握住不断的那条旋律。

normal.en: The musical tenor and the everyday tenor are the same word: one holds a note, the other holds a meaning.
normal.cn: 音乐上的 tenor 与日常的 tenor 是同一个词：一个握住音符，一个握住意思。

normal.en: Tenable, tenacity, tenant and tenure share the root, so a whole family gathers around holding.
normal.cn: tenable、tenacity、tenant、tenure 同根，一整族词都围绕「握住」。

normal.en: The tenor of a discussion is the way the talk is going, whether calm or angry.
normal.cn: the tenor of a discussion 指谈话的走向，平静还是愤怒。

normal.en: In law, the tenor of a deed is the intent that actually operates, not the literal words.
normal.cn: 法律上，契约的 tenor 是真正起作用的意图，而不是字面的字句。

abstract.en: Picture a single spun thread pulled from the first word to the last, and its slope is the tenor.
abstract.cn: 想象一根从第一个词拉到最后一个词的细线，这根线的斜度就是 tenor。

abstract.en: Hear a high male voice holding one long note while the other parts come and go.
abstract.cn: 想象一个高亢的男声握住一个长音，其他声部来了又走。

abstract.en: Think of a meeting room whose air changes: the words stay, but the tenor has turned.
abstract.cn: 回想一间气氛变了的会议室：话没有变，tenor 却转了个向。

examples.en: The tenor of her reply suggested she was not surprised.
examples.cn: 她回复的语气显示出她并不意外。

examples.en: A young tenor sang the leading role in the concert.
examples.cn: 一位年轻男高音在音乐会上唱了主角。

examples.en: The whole tenor of the city changed when the factory closed.
examples.cn: 工厂关闭后，这座城市的整体基调变了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「特诺」——男高音特意许诺唱完整首，一个音都不放，就是「持续不断的主线」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 tenere（握住、延续）→ 拉丁语名词 tenor（连续的进程；曲调或言辞的走向）→ 古法语 tenor → 英语 tenor。同根词：tenable、tenacity、tenant、tenure。中世纪音乐把「保持旋律」的声部称作 tenor，声部义由此而来。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of tenor all follow one held line: an unbroken course, then its overall meaning, then the voice and parts that hold the melody, and finally the intent a document holds.
sensesIntro.cn: tenor 的五个义项都沿着同一条被握住的线走：不间断的进程，接着是它的整体意味，然后是「握住」旋律的嗓音与声部，最后是文件所握住的意图。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one voice holds a long note from the first bar to the last, and the others follow it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个声音从第一小节到最后一小节握住一个长音，其他声部都跟着它。

branches.en: THE COURSE: the most literal carry-over of Latin tenor, a continuous line that something runs along.
branches.cn: 进程线：拉丁语 tenor 最直白的延续，指某事物沿着走的连续的一条线。

branches.en: THE MEANING: once the line is a speech or a text, its overall direction becomes the sense the word carries most often.
branches.cn: 意义线：当这条线是演讲或文字时，它的整体走向就成了这个词最常见的义项。

branches.en: THE VOICE: medieval music gives the name to the part that holds the melody, and it settles on the highest male voice.
branches.cn: 嗓音线：中世纪音乐把这个名字给了保持旋律的声部，后来固定指最高的男声。

branches.en: THE RANGE: any part or instrument built for that range borrows the name, from choir parts to the tenor saxophone.
branches.cn: 音域线：凡是按这个音域写成的声部或乐器都借用了这个名字，从合唱声部到次中音萨克斯。

branches.en: THE INTENT: a legal text also holds a purpose, and law calls the purpose that operates its tenor.
branches.cn: 意图线：法律文本同样握着一个目的，法律把实际起作用的目的称为它的 tenor。

intro.en: Tenor is a Latin noun made from a holding verb with the agent ending -or; English adds nothing but the plural and a few rare compounds.
intro.cn: tenor 是拉丁语「握住」动词加施动词尾 -or 构成的抽象名词；英语只加复数与少数罕见复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin tenere and tenor are both recorded, and the medieval musical use is documented in its own right.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tenere 与 tenor 均有文献记录，中世纪的音乐用法也有独立文献可查。

items.example: The verb supplies the holding image.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供「握住」的意象。

items.meaning: a continuous course, the drift of a speech
items.meaningCN: 连续的进程；话语的走向
items.example: The noun is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是英语词形的直接来源。

items.meaning: one who does, or the doing itself
items.example: It builds the noun from the holding verb.
items.exampleCN: 它把这个名词建立在「握住」动词之上。

items.example: It forms tenors.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 tenors。

items.example: It forms tenorist.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 tenorist。

items.example: Tenable shares the same holding root.
items.exampleCN: tenable 共享同一「握住」词根。

items.example: Tenacity comes from Latin tenax.
items.exampleCN: tenacity 来自拉丁语 tenax。

items.example: Tenant is a person who holds.
items.exampleCN: tenant 就是「持有」的人。

items.example: Tenure repeats the holding idea.
items.exampleCN: tenure 重复了「握住」这一念头。

definition_zh: 抗拉的；张力的；拉伸用的
definition_en: relating to pulling or stretching, especially the ability of a material to resist being pulled apart
core_image: 一根钢索被两头对拉，绷得笔直却不被拉断
scene: 桥梁设计师在吊索旁弯下腰，测试钢材两端的抗拉强度。Beside the cable, the bridge designer wrote down the tensile strength of the steel.
sceneCN: 这里 tensile 是「抗拉的」（第 1 个义项：材料承受拉力而不被拉断的能力）；句意：桥梁设计师在吊索旁弯下腰，测试钢材在两端拉紧时的强度。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 tensio 而来，由动词 tendere 派生，义为「张力；紧张」
tens- 加 -ible 构成，义为「可被拉伸的」

senses.title: Relating to pulling
senses.definition: relating to or involving a force that pulls something apart, especially a material capable of resisting it
senses.definitionCN: 涉及把某物拉开的力量，尤指材料能承受这种拉力而不断裂
senses.example: Steel has a very high tensile strength.
senses.exampleCN: 钢材的抗拉强度非常高。
senses.why: The Latin stem tens- means stretched, so the word names exactly the state of being pulled from both ends.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词干 tens- 意为「被拉紧」，所以这个词直接指向两端被拉扯的状态，这正是材料抗拉试验的核心画面。

senses.title: Caused by pulling
senses.titleCN: 拉力造成的；张力引起的
senses.definition: caused by or resulting from forces that stretch a body, as in tensile stress or tensile failure
senses.definitionCN: 由使物体伸长的拉力造成或引起的，如拉应力或拉伸断裂
senses.example: The pipe cracked under tensile stress.
senses.exampleCN: 管道在拉应力作用下裂开了。
senses.why: Once the word describes the force rather than the material, it can label any damage or deformation that pulling produces.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词从描述材料转到描述力本身，它就能标记一切由拉扯造成的损伤或变形，所以断裂、裂纹都可以叫 tensile。

senses.title: Stretched or ductile
senses.titleCN: 有延展性的；能被拉长的
senses.definition: capable of being drawn out or extended by pulling, as wire or filament
senses.definitionCN: 能够通过拉扯被拉长或抽细的，如金属丝或纤维
senses.example: Silver is the most tensile metal used for thin wire.
senses.exampleCN: 银是用于制作细导线的金属中延展性最强的。
senses.why: A material that can be drawn into wire is literally stretched thin, so the pulling image turns into a property of the material itself.
senses.whyCN: 能被抽成丝的金属事实上就是被一点点拉细的，于是「拉扯」的画面沉淀为材料自身的性质，即延展性。

senses.title: Tensile architecture
senses.definition: describing structures held up by elements under tension, such as cables or membranes
senses.definitionCN: 指依靠缆索或膜材等受拉构件支撑起来的结构
senses.example: The stadium roof is a striking example of tensile architecture.
senses.exampleCN: 体育场的屋顶是张拉结构的一个醒目范例。
senses.why: Modern engineering builds roofs that hang from cables, so the word moved from steel fibres to whole buildings held in tension.
senses.whyCN: 现代工程用悬索吊起屋顶，词义便从钢纤维扩展到整座由拉力撑起的建筑，建筑术语里就有张拉结构一说。

senses.title: In the tensile test
senses.definition: denoting the standard mechanical test that pulls a specimen until it yields or breaks
senses.definitionCN: 指把试样一直拉伸到屈服或断裂的标准力学试验
senses.example: Each batch of concrete goes through a tensile test.
senses.exampleCN: 每一批混凝土都要经过拉伸试验。
senses.why: Laboratory method names are built on the force being applied, and a tensile test is simply the pulling version of testing.
senses.whyCN: 实验室的方法名以所施加的力命名，拉伸试验就是「拉扯版」的测试，因此 tensile 自然成为试验的名称前缀。

senses.title: In biology
senses.definition: describing the strength, flexibility or pull exerted by living tissues such as tendons
senses.definitionCN: 描述肌腱等活体组织的强度、柔韧度或所承受的牵拉
senses.example: Tendons have remarkable tensile strength for their size.
senses.exampleCN: 肌腱相对于其体积具有惊人的抗拉强度。
senses.why: Muscles and tendons work by pulling, so biologists borrowed the engineering word to describe how tissue resists being torn.
senses.whyCN: 肌肉与肌腱本就靠拉开工作，生物学家借用工程术语来描述组织不易被撕裂，这个义项是第 1 个义项的生物学延伸。

senses.title: Opposed to compressive
senses.definition: forming the half of a material description that involves stretching, as opposed to squeezing
senses.definitionCN: 在与压缩相对的对比中，指涉及拉伸的那一半材料描述
senses.example: Textbooks discuss tensile and compressive forces side by side.
senses.exampleCN: 教科书把拉力和压力并排讨论。
senses.why: Physics pairs pulling with pushing, so tensile became one half of a fixed contrast with compressive.
senses.whyCN: 物理学把「拉」与「压」成对处理，tensile 因此固定地充当与抗压相对的那一半说法。

senses.title: Figurative strain
senses.definition: used loosely for situations or relationships that feel stretched and strained
senses.definitionCN: 松散地用于形容被拉得很紧、令人紧张的情境或关系
senses.example: The team wrote about the tensile pressure of a tight deadline.
senses.exampleCN: 团队写到紧迫截稿期带来的紧绷压力。
senses.why: The physical image of a taut wire is easily transferred to nerves, schedules and teams, giving a figurative strain sense.
senses.whyCN: 绷紧的钢丝最容易联想到神经、日程和团队，于是物理的拉力画面被转用到情绪与关系上，长出比喻义的紧绷。

intro.en: Tensile comes from Latin tendere, to stretch, through the Late Latin noun tensilis, meaning that can be stretched.
intro.cn: tensile 来自拉丁语 tendere（拉伸），经晚期拉丁语形容词 tensilis（可被拉伸的）进入英语。

items.cn: 动词 tendere 意为拉开、伸展或撑起帐篷。

items.en: The adjective tensilis means capable of being stretched.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语形容词 tensilis 意为能被拉伸的。

items.en: English borrows the word as tensile for things related to stretching.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 tensile，表示与拉伸有关。

items.en: Engineers standardise tensile strength, tensile test and tensile stress as fixed technical terms.

items.en: The word spreads to biology, textile design and tensile architecture.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到生物学、纺织设计与张拉建筑。

note.en: Tensile belongs to the family of tendere, with tense, tension and attention; it neighbours words for stretching and for strength.
note.cn: tensile 属于 tendere 词族，与 tense、tension、attention 同源；在意义上与「拉伸」和「强度」类词相邻。

senses.title: Thin and delicate
senses.definition: very thin, fine or delicate, so that it is easily broken or seen through
senses.definitionCN: 非常细、非常薄或精致，因而容易被折断或被看穿
senses.example: A tenuous thread of smoke rose from the candle.
senses.exampleCN: 一缕纤细的烟从蜡烛上升起。
senses.why: Latin tenuis simply means thin, so the physical thinness of a thread or a thread of smoke is the literal core.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 tenuis 本义就是「薄、细」，所以丝线或一缕烟的物理纤薄，就是这个字最字面的核心。

senses.title: Weak or slight
senses.definition: weak or slight in amount, especially for support, evidence or sound
senses.definitionCN: 在数量上微弱或单薄，尤指支撑、证据或声音方面
senses.example: The proposal rests on tenuous support.
senses.exampleCN: 这项提议只靠薄弱的支持撑着。
senses.why: When something thin is used as support, it cannot hold much weight, so thinness becomes weakness.
senses.whyCN: 东西一薄，就撑不住重量；当纤细被用作支撑时，自然引申为支持量微薄，由物理之薄过渡到力量之弱。

senses.title: Frail or insecure
senses.definition: fragile and easily lost or broken, as a position or a peace
senses.definitionCN: 脆弱且容易失去或打破的，如地位或和平
senses.example: The rebel leader held tenuous control of the city.
senses.exampleCN: 叛军首领对这座城市只有脆弱的控制。
senses.why: A thin hold means fingers barely closed around the object, so the word pictures power or peace about to slip away.
senses.whyCN: 薄的一握意味着手指几乎没合拢，于是这个词直接画出权力或和平随时会滑走的危局，脆弱感由此而来。

senses.title: Hardly a link at all
senses.definition: so slight that a link, relationship or connection is barely there
senses.definitionCN: 微弱到几乎不存在的联系、关系或牵连
senses.example: There is only a tenuous link between the two reports.
senses.exampleCN: 两份报告之间只有薄弱的联系。
senses.why: A thread between two points can be stretched until it is almost invisible, which is exactly how a slight relationship feels.
senses.whyCN: 两点之间的一根线能被拉细到几乎看不见，人际意义上的微弱联系，用的正是这个画面。

senses.title: Weakly argued
senses.definition: used for reasoning or evidence too thin to convince a reader
senses.definitionCN: 用于形容过于单薄、难以说服读者的推理或证据
senses.example: His conclusion is a tenuous stretch of the evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 他的结论只是对证据的牵强延伸。
senses.why: Logic is judged by how much weight it can bear, so reasoning that is thin is called tenuous just as a weak rope is.
senses.whyCN: 论证要看它能承重多少，推理一薄就是牵强，这与绳子一细就易断出于同一种量薄的判断。

senses.title: Faint and thin in air
senses.definition: thin or rare in a physical sense, as the atmosphere at great height
senses.definitionCN: 物理意义上稀薄，如高空中的大气
senses.example: The guides breathed tenuous air near the summit.
senses.exampleCN: 向导们在接近峰顶处呼吸着稀薄的空气。
senses.why: This keeps the literal Latin sense: air with fewer molecules per breath is air that has been thinned out.
senses.whyCN: 这里保留了拉丁语的字面义：每口气分子更少的空气就是被摊薄了的空气，所以稀薄与纤细同源。

senses.title: Slight in amount
senses.definition: very slight in degree, used of sounds, chances or differences
senses.definitionCN: 在程度上极轻的，用于声音、机会或差别
senses.example: Only a tenuous difference separates the two shades.
senses.exampleCN: 两种色调之间只有细微的差别。
senses.why: Scale follows the thin thread image: the thinner the gap, the smaller the margin of proof we are talking about.
senses.whyCN: 程度量也用细线的画面来想：缝隙越细，可争的余地越小，于是引申出某一差别或机会极为轻微。

senses.title: Stretched into a line
senses.definition: describing something drawn out thin and long, as a filament or a sliver
senses.definitionCN: 描述被拉得又细又长的东西，如细丝或细片
senses.example: The spider drew a tenuous line across the doorway.
senses.exampleCN: 蜘蛛在门口拉出一根细长的线。
senses.why: The thinness of a fibre comes from being drawn out, so the adjective also captures the moment a substance is stretched to its limit.
senses.whyCN: 纤维的细往往是被拉出来的，所以这个词也能捕捉物质被拉到极限那一刻的状态，即细长拉丝的样子。

intro.en: Tenuous comes from Latin tenuis, meaning thin, fine or slight, and still keeps that threadlike image.
intro.cn: tenuous 直接来自拉丁语 tenuis（薄的、细的、轻微的），至今保留着「细丝」般的画面。

items.en: A reconstructed root ten- gives the idea of stretching thin.
items.cn: 一般认为重构词根 ten- 含有「拉薄」的概念。

items.en: The adjective tenuis means thin, slender, delicate or slight.
items.cn: 拉丁语形容词 tenuis 意为薄、细、纤细或轻微。

items.en: Scientific Latin revives tenuis as tenuis or tenuous for fine structure.
items.cn: 十七世纪的拉丁学术语以 tenuis 或 tenuous 表示细致结构。

items.en: English adopts tenuous for thin, fine and delicate things.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪引入 tenuous，用于纤细、精致的事物。

items.en: The word shifts toward weakness of argument, support or connection.
items.cn: 词义转向论证、支撑或联系的薄弱。

items.en: News writing uses tenuous for fragile links, holds and diplomatic ties.
items.cn: 当代新闻写作常用 tenuous 形容脆弱的联系、掌控与外交关系。

note.en: Tenuous is the adjective of thinness, beside attenuate, tenuity and the near meanings flimsy, slim and fragile.
note.cn: tenuous 是表示「细薄」的形容词，与 attenuate、tenuity 同源；在意义上与 flimsy、slim、fragile 相邻。

branches.en: A link stretched almost to nothing.

branches.en: Thin reasoning and slight degrees of difference.
branches.cn: 单薄的论证与极轻微的差别。

branches.en: Thin air and a filament drawn into a line share the literal image.
branches.cn: 稀薄的空气与被拉成的细线共享同一字面画面。

intro.en: Tenuous is built from Latin tenu-, from tenuis meaning thin, plus the adjectival ending -ous.
intro.cn: tenuous 由拉丁语 tenu-（源自 tenuis，薄的）加形容词词尾 -ous 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin tenuis means thin or slight; the stem tenu- plus -ous gives tenuous, and tenuis also feeds attenuate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tenuis 意为细薄、轻微；词干 tenu- 加 -ous 构成 tenuous，tenuis 还衍生出 attenuate。

definition_zh: 微温的；不冷不热的；不热情的
definition_en: only slightly warm, or showing little interest or enthusiasm
core_image: 一杯放了太久的洗澡水，手指探进去只有一点点余温
scene: 汤端上桌时已经放凉，尝起来只剩微温。By the time the soup reached the table it had cooled to a tepid state.
sceneCN: 这里 tepid 是「微温的」（第 1 个义项：只比室温略暖、几乎没有热度）；句意：汤端上桌时已经放凉，尝起来只剩微温。

derivatives.zh: tepid 加 -ity 构成，义为「微温；冷淡」
tepid 加 -ly 构成，义为「不温不火地；冷淡地」
tepid 加 -ness 构成，义为「不冷不热的性质」

senses.title: Slightly warm
senses.definition: only slightly warm, as a liquid close to room temperature
senses.definitionCN: 只比常温略暖，如接近室温的液体
senses.example: She washed the cut with tepid water.
senses.exampleCN: 她用微温的水清洗了伤口。
senses.why: The Latin source tepidus literally means lukewarm, and the physical temperature sense has never been lost.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 tepidus 本义就是「不冷不热」，所以物理温度的义项从未丢失，是这个词最基础的用法。

senses.title: Neither hot nor cold
senses.definition: lacking either heat or chill, and therefore unremarkable as a temperature
senses.definitionCN: 既没有热度也没有凉意，因此温度平淡无奇
senses.example: The bath water was tepid and disappointing.
senses.exampleCN: 洗澡水不冷不热，让人失望。
senses.why: Lukewarm is defined by what it lacks at both ends, so the word draws attention to a temperature that satisfies no one.
senses.whyCN: 微温的特点在于两头都不具备，所以这个词总能带出「谁也不满意」的意味，温度上的缺席感正是它被反复使用的理由。

senses.title: Unenthusiastic
senses.definition: showing little enthusiasm, interest or support
senses.definitionCN: 表现出很少的热情、兴趣或支持
senses.example: The plan met with a tepid reaction from the council.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会对这项计划反应冷淡。
senses.why: Warmth is a standard metaphor for enthusiasm, so a temperature that is merely tepid signals feeling that has cooled but not frozen.
senses.whyCN: 温度系统常被用来比喻热情，因此仅剩微温的形容自然指向「热度已退却尚未冷却」的态度，即不冷不热。

senses.title: A cold reception
senses.definition: used of an audience, a crowd or a host whose welcome is polite but flat
senses.definitionCN: 用于形容听众、观众或主人礼貌却寡淡的欢迎
senses.example: The singer got a tepid reception at the small club.
senses.exampleCN: 这位歌手在小俱乐部遭到了冷淡的接待。
senses.why: Applause is judged by heat, so a crowd that claps lightly gives the performer a response that is only lukewarm.
senses.whyCN: 掌声常用热度来衡量，观众轻轻拍手的反应就是微温的回应，这个义项专门描写「有礼但寡淡」的场合。

senses.title: Flat and bland
senses.definition: describing food, drink or writing that is dull and lacks bite
senses.definitionCN: 形容饮食或文字寡淡、缺乏锐利感
senses.example: The tepid reviews did little to help ticket sales.
senses.exampleCN: 那些平淡的评论对票房帮助不大。
senses.why: A lukewarm drink loses its edge, and the same loss of sharpness is applied to reviews, jokes and prose.
senses.whyCN: 温吞的饮品会失去爽口之感，评论、笑话与文字失去尖锐感时，也用同一个「不冷不热」来描写，故派生平淡。

senses.title: Half hearted
senses.titleCN: 不温不火的；半心半意的
senses.definition: done or offered without firm conviction or effort
senses.definitionCN: 在缺乏坚定信念或投入的情况下做出或给出的
senses.example: He offered only tepid support for the new policy.
senses.exampleCN: 他对新政策只表示不温不火的支持。
senses.why: Support that neither warms nor cools shows someone who has not decided, so tepid marks half hearted commitment.
senses.whyCN: 既不加温也不降温的支持，说明人还没拿定主意，于是这个词标记出半心半意的承诺。

senses.title: In medicine
senses.definition: technical use for a liquid or a bath that should be lukewarm for medical care
senses.definitionCN: 技术用法，指护理中应当使用温凉的液体或沐浴
senses.example: Patients were advised to try a tepid sponge bath.
senses.exampleCN: 医生建议病人尝试微温的海绵擦浴。
senses.why: Medical care often needs water between cold and hot, and the word keeps its precise lukewarm force in that setting.
senses.whyCN: 护理往往需要冷热之间的水，这个词在医学语境中保留了最精确的「不冷不热」之力，所以成了一个专业说法。

senses.title: Economically slack
senses.definition: describing markets or demand that are weak without being collapsed
senses.definitionCN: 形容市场或需求疲软但尚未崩盘
senses.example: Sales were tepid through the spring quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 整个春季季度的销售都很低迷。
senses.why: Prices and demand are spoken of as hot or cold, so a market that is neither shows the same lukewarm image applied to money.
senses.whyCN: 行情常用冷热来表述，既不火热也不冰冷的市场，正是把「微温」的画面落实到金钱上，因而表示疲软。

intro.en: Tepid comes from Latin tepidus, lukewarm, from tepere, to be warm or mildly hot.
intro.cn: tepid 来自拉丁语 tepidus（温热的），源于动词 tepere（温热、略有热感）。

items.en: A reconstructed root tep- contributes the idea of being warm.
items.cn: 一般认为存在重构词根 tep-，含有「温热」的概念。

items.en: The verb tepere means to be warm, and tepidus means lukewarm.
items.cn: 拉丁语动词 tepere 意为温热，形容词 tepidus 意为不冷不热。

items.en: Medieval Latin and Old French forms such as tede carry the lukewarm word into the north.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语与古法语中的 tede 等词形把「微温」一词带到北方。

items.en: English borrows tepid from Latin for water that is only slightly warm.
items.cn: 英语在十五至十六世纪从拉丁语借入 tepid，指略温的水。

items.en: Nineteenth and twentieth century writers extend tepid to feelings and public responses.
items.cn: 十九与二十世纪的作家把 tepid 扩展到情感与公众反应。

items.en: The word now covers reviews, support, markets and diplomacy.
items.cn: 如今它覆盖评论、支持、市场与外交等语境。

note.en: Tepid keeps the Latin warmth root tep-, and sits beside lukewarm and the cool cues of enthusiasm.
note.cn: tepid 保留拉丁语「温热」词根 tep-，在意义上与 lukewarm 以及表示热情冷却的词相邻。

normal.en: Tepid water is warm enough to wash but not to steam.
normal.cn: tepid water 温到可以洗，却不会冒蒸汽。

normal.en: A tepid response means the room barely reacted.

normal.en: Tepere is the Latin verb for being warm.

normal.en: Tepid support is support without conviction.

normal.en: Lukewarm is the most common everyday synonym.

examples.cn: 服务员倒上微温的茶，并为上菜太慢道歉。

examples.en: The film received tepid reviews from the local critics.
examples.cn: 这部影片在当地评论界反应不温不火。

examples.en: Her enthusiasm for the club grew tepid after the first month.
examples.cn: 一个月之后她对俱乐部的热情就淡了。

sensesIntro.en: Tepid moves from a temperature between warm and cool to the same in-between state of enthusiasm, reception, writing and markets.
sensesIntro.cn: tepid 从冷热之间的温度，过渡到热情、接待、文字与市场上的「不冷不热」状态。

branches.en: Between two temperatures, and the medical use of that middle.

intro.en: Tepid joins the Latin root tep- for being warm with the adjectival ending -id, and adds -ity, -ly and -ness in English.
intro.cn: tepid 用拉丁词根 tep-（温热）加形容词词尾 -id 构成，英语中再加 -ity、-ly、-ness。

latinIntro.en: Latin tepere means to be warm, and tepidus adds -idus to form the adjective lukewarm.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tepere 意为温热，tepidus 加 -idus 构成形容词「微温的」。

definition_zh: 术语；专业词汇；术语学
definition_en: the set of technical words and expressions used in a particular subject, or the study of such words
core_image: 一张写满专业标记的标签板，每个标签只对应一个精确概念
scene: 读医学论文时，满篇专业术语让读者不得不先查词典。Readers of a medical paper must often look up long lists of technical terminology.
sceneCN: 这里 terminology 是「专业术语」（第 1 个义项：某一领域的专门用语）；句意：读医学论文时，满篇专业术语让读者不得不先查词典。

collocations.zh: 术语空白；专业词汇缺口

derivatives.zh: 术语（该词去除后缀后留下的词根名词，义为专门用语）
末端的；终点的（与 terminus 同源于「边界」）
终止；结束（同源于拉丁语终止义）
术语的；术语学的（terminology 去 -y 加 -ical 构成）

senses.title: Technical vocabulary of a field
senses.definition: the technical words and expressions used by people working in a particular subject
senses.definitionCN: 某一领域的人使用的专门术语和表达
senses.example: The report is full of legal terminology.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告满是法律术语。
senses.why: The accountancy of a field needs exact names, so terminology became the word for that exact set of names.
senses.whyCN: 一个领域需要精确的名号，所以 terminology 成了「这套精确名称」的总称。

senses.title: The body of terms as a system
senses.definition: the whole structured system of terms a discipline has agreed to use
senses.definitionCN: 某个学科约定使用的一整套结构化术语
senses.example: Scientists from different countries agreed on a shared terminology.
senses.exampleCN: 不同国家的科学家就一套通用术语达成一致。
senses.why: Beyond single words, the word names the whole network of labels that a discipline holds in common.
senses.whyCN: 除了单个词，这个词还指整个学科共同持有的标签网络。

senses.title: The study of specialized terms
senses.definition: the academic study of how specialized terms are formed, defined, and used
senses.definitionCN: 研究专门术语如何形成、定义和使用的学科
senses.example: She teaches terminology at a translation school.
senses.exampleCN: 她在一所翻译学院教术语学。
senses.why: The suffix -logy marks a field of study, so the word also names the discipline of collecting and standardizing terms.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -logy 表示学科，所以这个词也指收集和规范术语的学问。

senses.title: Jargon that outsiders cannot follow
senses.titleCN: 行话；外人听不懂的用词
senses.definition: language so loaded with technical terms that people outside the field cannot follow it
senses.definitionCN: 充满专业词、外行难以理解的语言
senses.example: Doctors should drop their terminology when talking to children.
senses.exampleCN: 医生跟孩子说话时应当少用行话。
senses.why: When the set of terms becomes a barrier instead of a tool, the word shifts into the mild complaint of jargon.
senses.whyCN: 当术语从工具变成障碍时，这个词就转成了对「行话」的温和抱怨。

senses.title: Formal naming used in formal documents
senses.definition: the special expressions used to name things precisely in official or academic writing
senses.definitionCN: 官方或学术写作中为精确指称而使用的特殊表达
senses.example: The treaty avoids vague wording by following a strict terminology.
senses.exampleCN: 这份条约用严格的术语避免含糊表述。
senses.why: Exact names protect legal meaning, so terminology also carries the flavour of careful official wording.
senses.whyCN: 精确的名称能保护法律含义，所以 terminology 也带有谨慎公文体用词的味道。

senses.title: Naming convention across industries
senses.definition: the convention that decides what a system, product, or process is officially called
senses.definitionCN: 决定某个系统、产品或流程正式叫什么的惯例
senses.example: The new app changed its terminology from users to members.
senses.exampleCN: 这款新应用把「用户」的说法改成了「会员」。
senses.why: Companies rename things to shape perception, and the agreed names they use form their terminology.
senses.whyCN: 公司通过改名来塑造印象，而它们一致采用的名称就构成其术语体系。

senses.title: A mismatch between names
senses.definition: a situation in which two groups use different terms for the same thing
senses.definitionCN: 两个群体对同一事物使用不同名称的情况
senses.example: Engineers and designers argued over terminology for weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师和设计师为叫法问题争论了数周。
senses.why: Because a system of names can clash, the word also appears in talk of terminology problems and gaps.
senses.whyCN: 因为命名体系可能冲突，这个词也出现在讨论术语问题与缺口的语境里。

senses.title: Specialist language as heritage
senses.titleCN: 术语积淀；学科的专门语汇
senses.definition: the inherited stock of technical expressions that a craft or science passes down
senses.definitionCN: 某一技艺或科学代代相传的专门表达储备
senses.example: The terminology of stone masonry survives in old manuals.
senses.exampleCN: 石匠工艺的术语在旧手册中保存下来。
senses.why: Old crafts hand their named tools and steps down, and this accumulated stock is also called terminology.
senses.whyCN: 老手艺把有名字的工具与工序传下去，这笔累积的语汇也叫 terminology。

intro.en: Terminology joins Greek terma, an end or limit, and logos, word or study.
intro.cn: terminology 由希腊语 terma（终点、界限）与 logos（言语、学问）组合而成。

items.en: Terminus Latinus means a boundary mark, still visible in the modern word terminus.
items.cn: 拉丁语 terminus 意为界石，这个意思在现代英语 terminus 中仍可见。

items.en: Terma means an end or limit, and logos means word or study.
items.cn: 希腊语 terma 意为终点或界限，logos 意为言语或学问。

items.en: The German compound Terminologie is recorded in the late eighteenth century.
items.cn: 德语复合词 Terminologie 在十八世纪后期有记录。

items.en: The word term is borrowed from Latin, meaning a boundary or the end of a period.
items.cn: term 借用自拉丁语，本义为界限或一段时间结束。

items.en: English terminology arrives in the early nineteenth century with the new sciences.
items.cn: 英语 terminology 在十九世纪初随新兴科学一起进入英语。

items.en: The precise coiner is uncertain, so the German origin is given as the accepted account.
items.cn: 具体造词者不确定，因此此处按公认说法以德语为来源。

note.en: Terminology belongs to the term family, and it sits beside words for jargon and vocabulary.
note.cn: terminology 属于 term 家族，与行话、词汇类词相邻。

entries.definition: a word or expression used for a particular thing
the final point or end of a route
forming the end of something
special words used by a group that others find hard to follow
all the words known to a person or used in a language
the system of names used in a science or branch of learning

normalIntro.en: Terminology is the boundary marks of a subject, giving each idea a precise edge.
normalIntro.cn: terminology 是一个学科的界石，为每个概念划出精确的边界。

normal.en: The root term comes from a Latin word for a boundary, so a term marks where a meaning ends.
normal.cn: 词根 term 来自表示「界限」的拉丁词，所以术语划出一层意思的终点。

normal.en: Terminology adds -logy, the suffix for a field of study, hence the study of such terms.
normal.cn: terminology 加上表示学科的 -logy，于是有「术语学」之义。

normal.en: Technical terminology is the fixed phrase for the specialized word stock.
normal.cn: technical terminology 是表示「专门词库」的固定搭配。

normal.en: Legal and medical terminology name two fields where exact words carry real weight.
normal.cn: legal terminology 与 medical terminology 说明这两个领域的精确用词影响重大。

normal.en: Compare nomenclature: nomenclature stresses naming systems, terminology stresses the words themselves.
normal.cn: 对比 nomenclature：nomenclature 强调命名系统，terminology 强调词语本身。

abstract.en: Picture every science branded with a row of brass tags.

abstract.en: Imagine a shared list of agreed names passed around a conference.

sensesIntro.en: Terminology starts as the set of technical words, extends to the system those words form, and finally names the study and the jargon problem.
sensesIntro.cn: terminology 先指专业词汇的集合，再扩展为这些词构成的体系，最后才指术语学以及行话带来的问题。

core.cn: 核心意象：一块记满精确铭牌的板子，每块铭牌只对应一个概念。

branches.en: The everyday sense is the word stock of a subject.
branches.cn: 最日常的义项是某一领域的词库。

branches.en: The system sense treats terms as a network.

branches.en: The study sense adds the -logy discipline.

latinEntries.meaning: to set a limit, to end

definition_zh: 终点站；终点；末端
definition_en: the end of a railway or bus line, or the final point of something
core_image: 铁轨的尽头立着一块界石，列车到此停住
scene: 绿皮车缓缓驶入终点站，乘客们纷纷起身拿行李。The old train rolled into its terminus and passengers reached for their bags.
sceneCN: 这里 terminus 是「终点站」（第 1 个义项：交通线路的终点）；句意：绿皮车缓缓驶入终点站，乘客们纷纷起身拿行李。

derivatives.zh: 终点站；航站楼（同源于 terminus 的「末端」义）
终止；结束（拉丁语 terminare 的英语承接形式）
终止；结束（terminate 加 -ion 构成）
术语；术语学（term 家族中最广为人知的成员）

senses.title: Last stop of a transport line
senses.definition: the station at the end of a railway, bus, or other route
senses.definitionCN: 铁路、公交或其他线路末端的车站
senses.example: The 5 bus has its terminus at the harbor.
senses.exampleCN: 五路公交的终点站在港口。
senses.why: The Roman boundary stone marks where a path stops, so the word came to name the end station of a route.
senses.whyCN: 罗马界石标记道路到此为止，所以这个词后来指线路尽头的车站。

senses.title: The final point of a process
senses.definition: the last point or stage that a process or journey reaches
senses.definitionCN: 过程或旅程所到达的最后一点或阶段
senses.example: The expedition finally reached its terminus in the desert.
senses.exampleCN: 探险队终于在沙漠中抵达终点。
senses.why: Any journey has a point where motion ends, and this abstract final point keeps the same image.
senses.whyCN: 任何旅程都有运动停止的一点，这个抽象的终点保留了同一意象。

senses.title: A statue of the boundary god
senses.definition: in Roman religion, the stone or statue marking a boundary, dedicated to the god Terminus
senses.definitionCN: 罗马宗教中立于边界、献给界神特尔米努斯的石块或雕像
senses.example: Each field had a small terminus crowned with flowers.
senses.exampleCN: 每块田地都立着一尊插着花的小界神像。
senses.why: The old Roman use was religious: a boundary stone honoured a god, and the word for it was the god name.
senses.whyCN: 古罗马用法带有宗教色彩：界石是献给神的，而这块石头的名字正是神名。

senses.title: An end point in computing
senses.definition: a point at which a program, data flow, or process stops
senses.definitionCN: 程序、数据流或进程停止的地方
senses.example: The compiler reports an error at the loop terminus.
senses.exampleCN: 编译器在循环的终止点报错。
senses.why: Technical writing reuses the boundary sense for any node where flow ends.
senses.whyCN: 技术写作把「边界」义借给任何流动终止的节点。

senses.title: A numeral marking an end
senses.definition: in Roman numerals, a sign used to mark the end of a number
senses.definitionCN: 罗马数字中用来标示数字结束的符号
senses.example: Later scribes added a terminus stroke to avoid fraud.
senses.exampleCN: 后来的抄写员加上终止笔画以防篡改。
senses.why: Ancient numbering needed a mark that a value was complete, and that mark was called the terminus.
senses.whyCN: 古代数字需要标记一个数值已经完整，这个标记就被叫 terminus。

senses.title: A final limiting condition
senses.definition: the ultimate limit that something can approach but not pass
senses.definitionCN: 某事物能够接近却不能越过的终极界限
senses.example: Death is not the terminus of every question.
senses.exampleCN: 死亡并不是所有问题的终极界限。
senses.why: A boundary stone marks a limit, and in learned writing the word keeps this abstract limit.
senses.whyCN: 界石标记界限，在一部分学理写作中这个词仍保留抽象的「极限」。

senses.title: An endpoint in a graph
senses.definition: a node at the end of an edge in a network diagram
senses.definitionCN: 网络图中一条边的末端节点
senses.example: Label the terminus of each branch before drawing the tree.
senses.exampleCN: 画树形图前先标出每个分支的端点。
senses.why: The frontier sense survives as the node where a path finishes in a diagram.
senses.whyCN: 「边界」义存留在图示中路径结束的节点上。

senses.title: The end of a protected area
senses.definition: the point that marks the outer limit of an area of land
senses.definitionCN: 标示一块土地外部边界的位置
senses.example: They planted oak posts along the terminus of the reserve.
senses.exampleCN: 他们沿着保护区的边界立起橡木桩。
senses.why: Stones mark where fields end, and the word still names the end marker of a parcel of land.
senses.whyCN: 石头标记田地的尽头，这个词至今也指一块土地的界标。

intro.en: Terminus is a Latin noun for a boundary stone, also the name of the Roman god of boundaries, and English took it as an end point.
intro.cn: terminus 是拉丁语中表示界石的名词，也是罗马界神之名，英语借来指终点。

items.en: Terminus means a boundary stone or a limit set on land.
items.cn: 拉丁语 terminus 意为界石，或为土地设下的界限。

items.en: The god Terminus guards boundary stones, and the stone itself carried that name.
items.cn: 界神特尔米努斯守护界石，石头本身就带着这个名字。

items.en: Poets use terminus for the end of a life or of a phase.
items.cn: 诗人在拉丁语中用 terminus 表示生命或阶段的终点。

items.en: English borrows terminus as an end or limit in learned writing.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 terminus，表示终点或界限。

items.en: Railways give the word its familiar sense of an end station.
items.cn: 十九世纪的铁路让这个词获得「终点站」这一熟悉含义。

items.en: The Latin sense of a limit is clear, but the older ancestor beyond Latin is uncertain.
items.cn: 拉丁语表示「界限」的意思是清楚的，但拉丁语之上更远的祖形尚不确定。

note.en: Terminus is the ancient boundary noun behind term, terminal, and terminology, and it sits near stop and endpoint words.
note.cn: terminus 是 term、terminal 与 terminology 背后的古老「界线」名词，与表示站点、终点的词相邻。

normalIntro.cn: terminus 是立在界限处的界石，因此指运动必须停下的地方。

normal.en: The shared root with term is visible: a term is also a boundary of a meaning.

normal.en: Terminal comes from the same word and means the end building of a line.

normal.en: Bus termini keep the frontier sense in everyday travel talk.

abstract.cn: 想象长句末尾的那个句号。

sensesIntro.en: Terminus begins as the stone marking a boundary, then names the station at the end of a route, and now serves as a general word for any final point.
sensesIntro.cn: terminus 最初指标示边界的石头，继而指线路尽头的车站，如今则泛指任何终点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone at the last rail, where the track stops.
core.cn: 核心意象：铁轨尽头那块让轨道停下的界石。

branches.en: The transport sense is the most familiar today.
branches.cn: 交通义是今天最熟悉的用法。

branches.en: The abstract sense keeps the final point of any journey.

branches.en: The religious sense shows the boundary stone as sacred.

branches.en: Technical senses turn the boundary into an end node.

branches.en: Marking an end in numbers or land shows the frontier image directly.
branches.cn: 用数字或土地标记终点直接体现「边界」意象。

definition_zh: 梯田；露台；阳台；排屋
definition_en: a flat paved area beside a building, a raised strip of land on a slope, or a row of joined houses
core_image: 山坡上层层叠起的平台，像被人踩出的巨大台阶
scene: 夕阳把山坡上的梯田染成金色，农夫正沿着田埂慢慢往上走。At sunset the terraces turned gold as the farmer climbed slowly along the paths.
sceneCN: 这里 terrace 是「梯田」（第 1 个义项：坡地上开出的阶梯状地块）；句意：夕阳把山坡上的梯田染成金色，农夫正沿着田埂慢慢往上走。

derivatives.zh: 阶梯状的；有露台的（terrace 加 -ed 构成）
梯田工程；阶梯地貌（terrace 加 -ing 构成）
地形；地势（同样来自拉丁语表示「土地」的词）
领土；地域（同源于拉丁语 terra 的家园义）

senses.title: A stepped plot on a hillside
senses.definition: one of a series of flat strips cut into a slope so that crops can be grown
senses.definitionCN: 在坡地上筑出的一级级平坦地块，用于耕种
senses.example: They grow rice on narrow terraces along the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在山谷两侧狭长的梯田上种水稻。
senses.why: The word comes from Latin terra, earth, plus a shape suffix, so a patch of shaped earth on a slope is its oldest image.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自拉丁语 terra（土地）加形状词尾，所以「坡地上被整形的土地」是最古老的意象。

senses.title: A paved level beside a building
senses.definition: a flat paved outdoor area next to a house, used for sitting or eating
senses.definitionCN: 房屋旁平坦的铺装户外区域，用于休憩或用餐
senses.example: We had breakfast on the terrace.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在露台上吃早餐。
senses.why: A levelled platform of earth beside a house keeps the same flat, raised shape as the hillside plot.
senses.whyCN: 屋旁一块平整的高出地面的地坪，与山坡地块一样平而略高。

senses.title: A balcony or roof area
senses.definition: a flat outdoor floor on a building, often on the roof or at a high level
senses.definitionCN: 建筑物上平坦的室外地面，常在屋顶或较高楼层
senses.example: The hotel has a terrace with a view of the bay.
senses.exampleCN: 酒店有一个能看见海湾的屋顶平台。
senses.why: A platform lifted to the top floor keeps the raised level of the hillside plot.
senses.whyCN: 平台被抬高到顶层，保留了山坡地块那种抬升的层级。

senses.title: A row of joined houses
senses.definition: one of a row of houses that are joined together, often sharing walls
senses.definitionCN: 一排相互连接的住宅之一，通常共用墙体
senses.example: They bought a small terrace near the station.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在车站附近买了一栋小排屋。
senses.why: Rows of houses built along a levelled street look like the stepped strips of a hillside, so the word was borrowed for the row.
senses.whyCN: 沿平整街道成排建起的房屋像山坡上的条条台地，于是这个词被借来描述这一排。

senses.title: A stepped bank stadium section
senses.definition: one of the stepped sections of seating in a sports ground
senses.definitionCN: 体育场中一排排阶梯状的座位区
senses.example: The east terrace was packed with singing fans.
senses.exampleCN: 东看台挤满了唱歌的球迷。
senses.why: Stepped seats rise like the steps of a hillside terrace, so crowds on those steps keep the same shape.
senses.whyCN: 阶梯座位像梯田的层层踏步一样升起，坐在上面的观众延续了这一形状。

senses.title: A geologically stepped bank
senses.definition: a flat shelf cut into a river bank or hillside by ancient water or movement
senses.definitionCN: 古代水流或地壳运动在河岸或山坡上切出的平坦台面
senses.example: Geologists traced four terraces along the river.
senses.exampleCN: 地质学家沿河追踪到四级阶地。
senses.why: Ancient rivers leave flat shelves in rock, and these shelves copy the farming steps exactly.
senses.whyCN: 古河流在岩石中留下平坦台面，这些台面与农田台阶形状完全一致。

senses.title: To shape land into steps
senses.titleCN: 筑梯田；把土地修成台阶
senses.definition: to cut a slope into flat steps, or to arrange something in level rows
senses.definitionCN: 把坡地修成平坦的台阶，或把东西排成层叠的行
senses.example: Farmers terraced the hillside to stop soil washing away.
senses.exampleCN: 农夫们把山坡修成梯田以防止泥土流失。
senses.why: The noun becomes a verb when people make the step themselves.
senses.whyCN: 当人们亲手造出这一层台阶时，名词就变成了动词。

senses.title: A small flat area for plants
senses.definition: a raised flat bed or shelf around a garden for plants
senses.definitionCN: 花园中用于种植的高起平坦苗床或花架
senses.example: Rose bushes line the terrace beside the path.
senses.exampleCN: 小径旁的种花台阶上排满玫瑰。
senses.why: A garden bed raised in one level is a small private version of the hillside terrace.
senses.whyCN: 抬升成一层的花床是山坡梯田的私人缩小版。

intro.en: Terrace comes from French terrasse, from Latin terra, earth, plus the shape suffix -aceus.
intro.cn: terrace 来自法语 terrasse，源于拉丁语 terra（土地）加形状后缀 -aceus。

items.en: Terra means earth or land, and terrasseus describes something made of earth.
items.cn: 拉丁语 terra 意为土地或大地，terrasseus 描述由土做成的事物。

items.en: Terraceus is used for pieces of ground raised in a stepped form.
items.cn: 中古拉丁语 terraceus 用来指被筑成阶梯状的土块。

items.en: Terrasse names a raised bank or a levelled platform of earth.
items.cn: 古法语 terrasse 指抬高的土坡或平整的土台。

items.en: English terrace first means a raised flat garden bank or walk.
items.cn: 英语 terrace 最初指花园中抬高的平土坡或步道。

items.en: The sense grows through roof and cafe platforms and into rows of town houses.
items.cn: 此后经由屋顶平台与咖啡馆露台扩展到成排的城镇住宅。

items.en: The precise first written use in English is uncertain, so the early date is given as general.
items.cn: 英语中确切的首见年代不确定，因此此处给出大致时段。

note.en: Terrace belongs to the earth family of terra and terrain, and it sits near words for balcony, plateau, and row houses.
note.cn: terrace 属于 terra 与 terrain 的「土地」词族，与阳台、台地、排屋类词相邻。

normal.cn: 对比 patio：patio 是铺装的院子，terrace 通常平整或抬升。

abstract.en: Picture a staircase of green fields climbing a hill.
abstract.cn: 想象一条由绿色田地铺成的阶梯爬上小山。

abstract.en: Imagine a cup of tea on a flat stone platform above a garden.
abstract.cn: 想象花园上方石台上的一杯茶。

abstract.en: Think of many identical brick houses standing shoulder to shoulder.
abstract.cn: 想象许多一模一样的砖屋并肩而立。

examples.en: The rice terraces have been farmed for centuries.
examples.cn: 这些稻田梯田已耕作数百年。

examples.en: Children played on the front terrace of the museum.
examples.cn: 孩子们在博物馆门前的平台上玩耍。

examples.en: She lives in a large terrace near the park.
examples.cn: 她住在公园附近一栋大的排屋里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「特拿斯」——特意把泥土一层层堆成台阶，就是梯田；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 terra（土地）+ 形状后缀 -aceus → 俗拉丁语 terraceus（土筑的阶梯平台）→ 古法语 terrasse → 英语 terrace，核心义「被整成一个层面的土地」。

sensesIntro.en: Terrace starts as a stepped strip of cultivated earth, widens to any flat platform beside a building, and then to rows of houses that repeat that level shape.
sensesIntro.cn: terrace 从坡地上耕作的阶梯地块出发，扩展到建筑旁任何平坦平台，再指重复这种层级形状的成排住宅。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a staircase of earth cut into a hillside.
core.cn: 核心意象：山坡上切出的一条泥土阶梯。

branches.en: The farm sense is the oldest and most concrete.
branches.cn: 农耕义最古老也最具体。

branches.en: Platform senses move the earth step up to a house roof.
branches.cn: 平台义把土地台阶挪到屋顶。

branches.en: Row and stand senses repeat the level strip in brick and seats.
branches.cn: 排屋与看台义用砖块和座位重复那一层条状结构。

branches.en: Geological traces keep the hillside step in natural rock.
branches.cn: 地质遗迹在天然岩石中保留山坡台阶。

branches.en: The verb turns the image into an action on land.
branches.cn: 动词义把意象变成对土地的改造动作。

intro.en: Terrace is built on Latin terra, with the shape suffix -aceus, and it shares its root with terrain and territory.
intro.cn: terrace 建立在拉丁语 terra 之上，带形状后缀 -aceus，并与 terrain、territory 共享词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin terra means earth, and terrasseus means made of earth or shaped as a bank.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 terra 意为土地，terrasseus 意为土筑的或筑成斜坡状的。

items.example: Terra is the base of terrace.
items.exampleCN: terra 是 terrace 的基底。

items.meaningCN: 表示「由……制成、具有……形态」的后缀
items.example: The suffix -aceus gives a made of earth sense.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -aceus 带来「由土制成」的意思。

items.example: Terrasse reaches English as terrace.
items.exampleCN: terrasse 以 terrace 的形式进入英语。

items.example: The terrace faces south.
items.exampleCN: 这个露台朝南。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms terraced.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 terraced。

items.example: Terraced fields cover the slope.
items.exampleCN: 梯田覆盖着山坡。

items.meaning: the building of steps in land
items.example: Terracing prevents erosion.
items.exampleCN: 修筑梯田可以防止侵蚀。

items.example: The terrain is rough.
items.exampleCN: 地形崎岖。

items.example: The territory is vast.
items.exampleCN: 这片领土辽阔。

items.example: Terrestrial plants need soil.
items.exampleCN: 陆生植物需要土壤。

definition_zh: 极好的；了不起的；极大的
definition_en: extremely good or enjoyable, or extremely great in amount or force; it keeps the Latin skeleton of terrifying, with the fear stem and the making suffix
core_image: 烟花在夜空炸开，人仰头看呆了
scene: 朋友家的聚会上，乐队临时加演了一首不在节目单上的歌，屋子里的气氛一下子被点燃。The band threw in an extra song and everyone agreed it was a terrific party.
sceneCN: 这里 terrific 是「极好的」（第 1 个义项：形容令人愉快、令人赞叹的事物）；句意：乐队临时多加了一首歌，大家都认为这是一场棒极了的聚会。

pos.zh: 形容词：极好的；了不起的；极大的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加后缀 -ally 构成，义为「极其；惊人地」
由拉丁词根 terr- 加动词后缀 -ify 构成，义为「使恐惧；吓唬」
由同一拉丁词根 terr- 加名词后缀 -or 构成，义为「恐惧；恐怖」
由形容词加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「极好的性质」，较为罕见

senses.title: Extremely good
senses.definition: so good, exciting, or impressive that it draws admiration
senses.definitionCN: 好到、精彩到让人赞叹的程度
senses.example: The show was terrific and the whole audience stood up.
senses.exampleCN: 演出棒极了，全场观众都站了起来。
senses.why: The old sense of causing terror was pushed to a peak of intensity, and modern speech reused that peak for approval.
senses.whyCN: 原义「引起恐惧」强调程度达到极点，现代口语把这个「极点」借用过来，就成了由衷的赞叹。

senses.title: Very large in amount
senses.definition: extremely great in size, amount, or degree
senses.definitionCN: 在规模、数量或程度上非常大
senses.example: The band faced a terrific amount of pressure in its first year.
senses.exampleCN: 这支乐队第一年承受了巨大的压力。
senses.why: The stem terr- marks something extraordinary, so adding it to a noun of quantity keeps the swelling, enlarging force.
senses.whyCN: 词干 terr- 标记「非同寻常」，加在表示数量的词上，就保留了那种不断鼓胀、放大的力量。

senses.title: Causing terror (old sense)
senses.definition: causing fear or terror, a sense now mostly found in older texts
senses.definitionCN: 引起恐惧或惊恐，这一用法如今多见于旧文献
senses.example: In old adventure stories a terrific storm often strikes the ship at night.
senses.exampleCN: 在古老的探险故事里，一场可怕的暴风雨常在夜里袭击船只。
senses.why: Latin terrificare means to make afraid, so the earliest English use of the word describes what frightens.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 terrificare 就是「使人害怕」，所以英语中最早的 terrific 描述的是令人恐惧的事物。

senses.title: Frighteningly powerful
senses.definition: so violent or powerful that it feels frightening
senses.definitionCN: 猛烈或强大到带有几分吓人
senses.example: The car hit the wall with terrific speed.
senses.exampleCN: 汽车以骇人的速度撞上了墙。
senses.why: Between the old sense and the modern praise stands a middle stage where sheer force itself is the impression.
senses.whyCN: 在旧义与今义之间还有一个中间阶段：让人记住的正是那股纯粹的力量，恐惧感被力量感覆盖。

senses.title: Of a very high degree in general
senses.definition: used informally as a strong degree word before a quality
senses.definitionCN: 口语中放在形容词前表示程度极强
senses.example: He was terrific at chess as a teenager.
senses.exampleCN: 他十几岁时象棋下得极好。
senses.why: Once the word no longer needs to name fear, it becomes a free intensifier that can praise any skill or quality.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词不再必须指向恐惧，它就变成一个自由的强调词，可以夸赞任何技能或品质。

intro.en: Terrific comes from Latin terrificus, from terrere, to frighten, plus -ficus, making, so it meant fear-making.
intro.cn: terrific 来自拉丁语 terrificus，由 terrere（使恐惧）加 -ficus（造成）构成，原义就是「造成恐惧的」。

items.en: Terrere means to frighten or terrify, and gives the terr- stem of terror.
items.cn: terrere 意为使恐惧、使惊恐，提供了 terror 的 terr- 词干。

items.en: The suffix -ficus comes from facere, to make, so terrificus means fear-making.
items.cn: 后缀 -ficus 源自 facere（做、造），因此 terrificus 意为「制造恐惧的」。

items.en: Scholars read Latin terrificus when naming a comet that seemed to threaten the sky.
items.cn: 十七世纪学者在给一颗仿佛威胁天空的彗星命名时，读到的是拉丁语 terrificus。

items.en: Early English terrific still means terrifying or dreadful.
items.cn: 早期英语的 terrific 仍表示「令人恐惧的、可怕的」。

items.en: Writers stretch it to great or mighty, and the fear fades while the size stays.
items.cn: 十九世纪作家长把它引申为「巨大的、有力的」，恐惧淡去，分量留下。

items.en: Twentieth-century speech moves the word to approval, and terrific becomes warm praise.
items.cn: 二十世纪口语把词义移到赞赏上，terrific 成了由衷的称赞。

note.en: Terrific belongs to the terr- family of fear words, and it now sits close to praise adjectives.
note.cn: terrific 属于 terr- 恐惧词族，如今又与一组表示赞誉的形容词相近。

extreme fear
very bad or frightening
entries.definitionCN: 糟糕的；可怕的；与 terrific 同源但走的是贬义一路

entries.definition: to shock and disgust
entries.definitionCN: 使震惊厌恶；horr- 词根不同，只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: extremely good
