abstract.en: Picture a torch going out in a dark corridor and your feet refusing to move.
abstract.cn: 想象黑暗走廊里手电突然熄灭，你的脚却迈不出去。

abstract.en: Imagine a criminal telling a shop owner that closing time matters.
abstract.cn: 想象一个歹徒对店主说，关门的时刻很重要。

abstract.en: Think of an exam hall where a single sheet on the desk looks enormous.
abstract.cn: 想象考场里桌上那张卷子显得无比巨大。

examples.en: The story of the old house used to terrify the village children.
examples.cn: 关于那座老房子的故事过去常把村里的孩子吓得不轻。

examples.en: I am terrified of speaking in front of a large audience.
examples.cn: 我非常害怕在很多人面前讲话。

examples.en: The sudden crash in the night terrified us all.
examples.cn: 夜里突然的撞击声把我们全吓坏了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「太瑞饭」——太吓人，饭都吃不下；这只是拆音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 terrere（使恐惧）+ -ficare（使……）→ terrificare（使害怕）→ 法语 terrifier → 英语 terrify，核心义「让人充满恐惧」。

sensesIntro.en: Terrify keeps one core action, making people afraid, and spreads it from direct fear to controlling fear, to frightening places, to dread of the future.
sensesIntro.cn: terrify 的核心动作始终是「让人害怕」，再由直接恐惧扩展到用恐惧控制、使地方可怕、对未来的忧惧。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shape steps out of the dark and your body freezes.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个影子从黑暗中走出，你的身体瞬间僵住。

branches.en: The plain sense is filling someone with intense fear.
branches.cn: 最直接的义项就是让人充满强烈的恐惧。

branches.en: Fear used as a tool becomes a sense of its own.
branches.cn: 恐惧被当作工具使用时，就长出了独立义项。

branches.en: Places and situations can carry the frightening quality too.
branches.cn: 地方与情形同样可以带上可怕的性质。

branches.en: Real danger and imagined danger trigger the same fear.
branches.cn: 真实的危险与想象的危险触发同一种恐惧。

branches.en: The passive turns the action into the lasting state of being terrified.
branches.cn: 被动式把动作转化成持续性的「被吓住」状态。

intro.en: Terrify is built from the Latin stem terr- plus the verb suffix -ify, which means to make.
intro.cn: terrify 由拉丁语词干 terr- 加表示「使……」的动词后缀 -ify 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin terrere and its participle territus supply the fear stem that runs through the whole terr- family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 terrere 及其分词 territus 提供了贯穿 terr- 词族的恐惧词干。

items.example: The root terr- is shared with terror and terrible.
items.exampleCN: 词根 terr- 与 terror、terrible 共享。

items.example: The suffix -ify turns the stem into a verb of making.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ify 把词干变成表示「使……」的动词。

items.example: Terrify names the act of putting fear into someone.
items.exampleCN: terrify 指把恐惧放进别人心里的动作。

items.example: Terrifying describes what causes the fear.
items.exampleCN: terrifying 描述引起恐惧的一方。

items.example: Terrified describes the person or animal that feels it.
items.exampleCN: terrified 描述感受到恐惧的人或动物。

items.example: Terror is the noun of the feeling itself.
items.exampleCN: terror 是这种恐惧感受本身的名词。

items.example: Terrorist adds a person suffix to the noun.
items.exampleCN: terrorist 在名词后加了表示「人」的后缀。

items.example: The prefix de- and the terr- stem build deterrent.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 de- 与 terr- 词干一起构成 deterrent。

items.example: Terrible keeps the same root with a different suffix.
items.exampleCN: terrible 保留同一词根，但后缀不同。

definition_zh: 恐吓；恫吓；使长期处于恐惧中
definition_en: to frighten people, often repeatedly and on purpose, so that they feel unsafe
core_image: 蒙面人挨家敲门吓唬，整条街不敢开灯
scene: 深夜的小巷里，几个醉汉拦住路过的学生，逼他们交出耳机又威胁不许报警。Neighbours say a small gang has been terrorising the lane for months.
sceneCN: 这里 terrorise 是「长期恐吓」（第 1 个义项：反复蓄意地让人恐惧）；句意：邻居们说有一小团伙已经在这条小巷恐吓了好几个月。

pos.zh: 及物动词：恐吓；恫吓；使长期处于恐惧中

derivatives.zh: 基础名词，由 terr- 加 -or 构成，义为「恐惧；恐怖」
由 terror 加后缀 -ism 构成，义为「恐怖主义」
由 terror 加表人后缀 -ist 构成，义为「恐怖分子」
由本词加 -ation 构成，义为「恐吓行为；恐吓状态」

senses.title: To frighten people repeatedly on purpose
senses.definition: to frighten a person or group again and again, usually on purpose
senses.definitionCN: 一再地、通常是有意地使某人或某群人害怕
senses.example: A few vandals had terrorised the street for weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 几个破坏者已经在街上恐吓了好几个星期。
senses.why: The noun terror, extreme fear, gains the verb suffix -ise, which means to put into a state, so the verb means to put people into terror.
senses.whyCN: 名词 terror 意为极度恐惧，加上表示「使进入某种状态」的动词后缀 -ise，就是「让人进入恐惧状态」。

senses.title: To control others through violence or threats
senses.titleCN: 以暴力或威胁迫人屈服
senses.definition: to force a person or group into obedience by violence or the threat of it
senses.definitionCN: 用暴力或暴力威胁使人服从
senses.example: The soldiers broke down doors to terrorise the captured town.
senses.exampleCN: 士兵们破门而入，用恐惧压服被占领的城镇。
senses.why: Because fear makes people obey, the verb also names the political act of using force to control a population.
senses.whyCN: 恐惧能让人听话，所以这个动词也指用武力控制一群人的政治行为。

senses.title: To make someone afraid of a thing
senses.definition: to frighten someone about something so that they avoid it
senses.definitionCN: 拿某件事吓唬某人，使其不敢去做
senses.example: Older workers terrorised new staff with stories of the night shift.
senses.exampleCN: 老员工用夜班的各种故事吓唬新员工。
senses.why: The suffix -ise allows the verb to frame any object, including a fear that is stirred up on purpose.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ise 让动词可以接各种宾语，包括被故意挑起的一种恐惧。

senses.title: To be badly frightened (passive)
senses.titleCN: 被吓得不敢出声（被动式）
senses.definition: in the passive, to live in fear because of someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 用于被动式，指因为某人或某事而一直生活在恐惧中
senses.example: The tenants were terrorised by late-night knocks at the door.
senses.exampleCN: 租客们被深夜的敲门声吓得整夜不安。
senses.why: The passive shows the lasting state, so the verb becomes an adjective for people who are kept in fear.
senses.whyCN: 被动式呈现的是一种持续状态，于是这个动词变成形容被人恐吓者的形容词性用法。

intro.en: Terrorise joins the noun terror, from Latin terror, with the French verb suffix -iser meaning to make.
intro.cn: terrorise 由名词 terror（源自拉丁语 terror）加上法语系动词后缀 -iser（使……）构成。

items.en: Terrere means to frighten, and the noun terror names the fear it produces.
items.cn: terrere 意为使恐惧，名词 terror 指由此产生的恐惧。

items.en: Old French terrour carries the noun into French and then into Middle English.
items.cn: 古法语 terrour 把这个名词带入法语，随后进入中古英语。

items.en: The suffix -iser makes verbs out of nouns and enters English as -ise and -ize.
items.cn: 后缀 -iser 由名词构成动词，以 -ise 或 -ize 的形式进入英语。

items.en: Terrorism names government rule by terror during the French Revolution.
items.cn: 法国大革命时期，terrorism 一词指以恐怖手段统治的政权行为。

items.en: Terrorise appears as a verb in its own right, meaning to fill with terror.
items.cn: terrorise 作为独立动词出现，意为「使充满恐惧」。

items.en: Today it usually describes bullying a group of people over a period of time.
items.cn: 如今它通常指在一段时间里反复欺凌一群人。

note.en: Terrorise builds on terror and sits among verbs of threatening and bullying rather than among simple fear words.
note.cn: terrorise 以 terror 为底，它的邻居是威胁与欺凌类动词，而不是单纯表达害怕的词。

entries.definition: extreme fear
extremely afraid
the use of violence for political ends
entries.definitionCN: 恐怖主义；与 terrorise 共底，但指成体系的行为

entries.definition: an area of land
entries.definitionCN: 领土；地区；terr- 词根来自土地而非恐惧，只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to say that harm will come
to frighten someone into doing or not doing something
to hurt or frighten weak people on purpose

normalIntro.en: Terrorise is terror turned into a verb: putting whole groups of people into a state of fear.
normalIntro.cn: terrorise 是把 terror 变成动词：把一群人推入恐惧状态。

normal.en: Terrorise takes the noun terror and adds the verb suffix -ise, meaning to make.
normal.cn: terrorise 取名词 terror，加表示「使……」的动词后缀 -ise。

normal.en: British spelling writes terrorise, while American spelling writes terrorize.
normal.cn: 英式拼写是 terrorise，美式拼写是 terrorize。

normal.en: The -ise suffix also builds modernise and summarise from nouns and adjectives.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ise 也把 modernise、summarise 从名词或形容词变成动词。

normal.en: Terrorise usually needs a group as its object, such as a street, a neighbourhood, or villagers.
normal.cn: terrorise 的宾语常是一群人，如一条街、一个社区或村民。

normal.en: Compare terror with terrorism: terror is the feeling, terrorism is an organised political method.
normal.cn: 对比 terror 与 terrorism：前者是感受，后者是有组织的政治手段。

abstract.en: Picture a masked figure knocking on every door in one long evening.
abstract.cn: 想象一个蒙面人在一个漫长的晚上挨家挨户敲门。

abstract.en: Imagine shop owners closing early not because of the weather but because of a gang.
abstract.cn: 想象店主提前关门，不是因为天气，而是因为一伙人。

abstract.en: Think of a family eating dinner with the curtains drawn, week after week.
abstract.cn: 想象一家人一周又一周地把窗帘拉上吃晚饭。

examples.en: The gang terrorised local business owners for years.
examples.cn: 那伙人多年来一直恐吓当地的店主。

examples.en: Do not let one loud neighbour terrorise the whole building.
examples.cn: 别让一个吵闹的邻居就吓得整栋楼不得安宁。

examples.en: Whole villages were terrorised into silence during the campaign.
examples.cn: 在那场运动期间，整个村庄都被吓得不敢出声。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「太惹来司」——太会惹事，把街坊都吓住；这只是拆音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 terrere（使恐惧）→ 名词 terror（极度恐惧）→ 加 -ise（使……进入某种状态）→ 英语 terrorise / 美式 terrorize，核心义「把恐惧施加给人」。

sensesIntro.en: Terrorise starts from the noun terror and keeps the action of putting people into fear, then narrows toward repeated bullying, control by force, and the lasting passive state.
sensesIntro.cn: terrorise 以名词 terror 为起点，保留「把人推入恐惧」的动作，再具体化为反复欺凌、以武力控制以及被动式的持续状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gang walking the same street night after night.
core.cn: 核心意象：一伙人夜复一夜地走上同一条街。

branches.en: Repeated, deliberate frightening is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 反复而蓄意的惊吓是日常义项。

branches.en: Force for political control is the public, political sense.
branches.cn: 为政治控制而使用武力是公共与政治义项。

branches.en: Using a scary story to warn someone off is the small-scale sense.
branches.cn: 用可怕的故事吓退别人是这个动词的小尺度用法。

branches.en: Both a gang and a tall tale can push people into fear.
branches.cn: 无论是团伙还是编出的故事，都能把人推进恐惧。

branches.en: The action of terrorising and the state of being terrorised mirror each other.
branches.cn: 恐吓的动作与被恐吓的状态互为镜像。

intro.en: Terrorise is the noun terror plus the verb suffix -ise, spelled -ize in American English.
intro.cn: terrorise 是名词 terror 加动词后缀 -ise 的产物，美式英语写作 -ize。

latinIntro.en: Latin terrere and the noun terror give the whole family its stem, and the suffix -ise travels into English through French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 terrere 与名词 terror 为整个词族提供词干，后缀 -ise 经法语进入英语。

items.example: The noun terror names the feeling the verb produces.
items.exampleCN: 名词 terror 正是这个动词所制造的感受。

items.meaning: to make, to cause to be
items.example: The suffix -ise turns terror into a verb of making.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ise 把 terror 变成表示「使……」的动词。

items.example: Terrorise is the British spelling of the verb.
items.exampleCN: terrorise 是该动词的英式拼写。

items.example: American usage prefers terrorize.
items.exampleCN: 美式英语更常用 terrorize。

items.example: Terrorised describes the community that suffers the fear.
items.exampleCN: terrorised 描述承受恐惧的群体。

items.meaning: the use of terror for political ends
items.example: Terrorism adds the noun suffix -ism.
items.exampleCN: terrorism 加了名词后缀 -ism。

items.example: Terrorist adds the person suffix -ist.
items.exampleCN: terrorist 加了表示人的后缀 -ist。

items.example: Terrify now competes with terrorise for the everyday sense.
items.exampleCN: terrify 如今在口语层面与 terrorise 分担「使害怕」。

items.example: The prefix de- and the terr- stem build deter and deterrent.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 de- 与 terr- 词干构成 deter 与 deterrent。

definition_zh: 第三的；第三级的；高等教育的；第三纪的；第三期的
definition_en: third in order, rank, or importance, or coming after the second stage in a process
core_image: 一列台阶走过头两级，脚落在第三级上才终于登到高处
scene: 报志愿时，老师把学校分成几个阶段来算，说多数学生要读到最后一个阶段才拿到职业资格。At the parents evening the tutor explained that most students reach the tertiary stage before they gain a professional qualification.
sceneCN: 这里的 tertiary 是「高等教育的」（第 1 个义项：完成中学之后的教育阶段）；句意：在家长会上，导师解释说多数学生要读到高等教育阶段才取得职业资格。

pos.zh: 第三的；第三级的；高等教育阶段的；第三纪的
第三级；第三位；第三纪（地层单位）

derivatives.zh: 每隔一天发作的；间日热的
三元的；三个一组的

senses.title: The stage after secondary schooling
senses.definition: relating to university or college education, the stage that follows secondary school
senses.definitionCN: 指大学或学院的、中学之后的教育阶段
senses.example: She hopes to go into tertiary education next year.
senses.exampleCN: 她希望明年进入高等教育阶段。
senses.why: Education is counted in stages, and the number three does not mean third rate here but third stage in a sequence.
senses.whyCN: 教育按阶段来数，这里的「第三」不是第三等，而是学习序列中的第三个阶段。

senses.title: Third in rank or order
senses.definition: coming third in a series of ranks, levels, or levels of care
senses.definitionCN: 在排名、层级或照护等级中排在第三位
senses.example: The burns unit is a tertiary referral centre for the whole region.
senses.exampleCN: 这家烧伤科是整个地区的三级转诊中心。
senses.why: The ordinal meaning is the plain dictionary sense, used wherever things are numbered one, two, three.
senses.whyCN: 序数本义是这个词典义的基础，凡按一二三排列的事物都可以用它。

senses.title: The service part of an economy
senses.definition: belonging to the sector of an economy that provides services rather than raw materials or manufacturing
senses.definitionCN: 指经济中提供服务的部门，而非原料或制造部门
senses.example: Tourism is a typical tertiary industry in coastal towns.
senses.exampleCN: 在沿海城镇，旅游业是典型的第三产业。
senses.why: Economists numbered the economy in three blocks, and the service block was the third one to be counted.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家把经济分成三大块来数，服务那一块被数在第三位。

senses.title: The third period of geological time
senses.definition: of the period of geological time between the end of the dinosaurs and the beginning of the Ice Age, a term now largely replaced in formal geology
senses.definitionCN: 指恐龙灭绝之后、冰河期之前那段地质年代，这一称谓在现代正式地质学中多数已被取代
senses.example: The hills are built of tertiary rocks laid down long before the ice sheets came.
senses.exampleCN: 这些丘陵由第三纪岩层构成，形成于冰盖到来之前很久。
senses.why: Geologists once counted the young rock layers in three, and the third number stuck to a whole era.
senses.whyCN: 早期地质学家把年轻的地层数了三层，第三个数字就固定成了一个时代的名称。

senses.title: A third level of care in medicine
senses.titleCN: 三级医疗的；三级预防的
senses.definition: describing the highest level of specialised care, or the last of three levels of prevention
senses.definitionCN: 指最高级别的专科医疗，或三段式预防中的最后一级
senses.example: Tertiary prevention aims to reduce the harm already caused by a disease.
senses.exampleCN: 三级预防的目的是减轻疾病已经造成的损害。
senses.why: Public health ranks care and prevention in levels, and the level numbered three is the last and most specialised.
senses.whyCN: 公共卫生把照料与预防分成等级，被数在第三的等级就是最后也最专门的一级。

senses.title: A third stage in a learning sequence
senses.definition: the third and most advanced stage of a course of study or training
senses.definitionCN: 学习或训练过程中第三个、也最进阶的阶段
senses.example: Our book is designed for learners moving into the tertiary phase of the course.
senses.exampleCN: 我们的教材面向进入课程第三阶段的学习者。
senses.why: Any long course can be cut into stages, and the stage numbered three marks the move towards mastery.
senses.whyCN: 任何长课程都能切成阶段，被数到第三的那一段标志着走向精通。

intro.en: Tertiary comes from Latin tertiarius, of the third, built on tertius, third, plus the suffix -arius.
intro.cn: tertiary 来自拉丁语 tertiarius（第三的、第三等的），由序数词 tertius（第三）加词尾 -arius 构成。

items.en: Tertius is the Latin ordinal number three, the word for third in a counted sequence.
items.cn: tertius 是拉丁语序数词「第三」，用来数序列中的第三项。

items.en: The suffix -arius means belonging to or connected with, and turns tertius into tertiarius.
items.cn: 词尾 -arius 表示「属于……、与……有关」，把 tertius 变成 tertiarius。

items.en: Tertiarius names a person or thing of the third rank, including a friar of the third order.
items.cn: tertiarius 指属于第三等级的人或物，其中包括第三会修士。

items.en: English borrows tertiary for a third rank or order, first in learned and church use.
items.cn: 英语借入 tertiary 表示第三等级或次序，最初见于学术与教会用语。

items.en: Geologists give the name to the rock series above the secondary, and a whole era follows.
items.cn: 地质学家把这个名字给了位于第二纪之上的岩系，一个地质时代随之得名。

items.en: Tertiary is now standard for university education, the service sector, and the third level of care.
items.cn: 现代英语中，tertiary 成了高等教育、服务部门与三级医疗的通用说法。

note.en: Group one holds the same Latin stem of third plus close -ary relatives; group two holds words that also name a later stage in a sequence.
note.cn: 第一组是同一个拉丁语「第三」词干及相近的 -ary 同族词；第二组是同样表示序列后段的词。

entries.definition: recurring every other day, as some fevers do
entries.definitionCN: 每隔一天发作的，如某些疟疾发热

entries.definition: made of three parts
of the fourth rank or order
coming after the primary and before the tertiary stage
entries.definitionCN: 第二的；中等的，位于初级与高等之间

entries.definition: the number after two
at a late, high level of development

normalIntro.en: Tertiary is the -ary number word built on Latin tertius, third, so it always asks what is being counted.
normalIntro.cn: tertiary 是由拉丁语 tertius（第三）加 -ary 构成的数词形容词，用它时总要问清是在数什么。

normal.en: Latin tertius means third, and -arius turns that number into an adjective.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 tertius 意为第三，-arius 把数词变成形容词。

normal.en: Tertiary education simply means study after school, not a third rate education.
normal.cn: tertiary education 就是中学之后的学习，不是「三流教育」。

normal.en: Say primary, secondary, tertiary when you list stages in order.
normal.cn: 按顺序列阶段时，说 primary、secondary、tertiary。

normal.en: In economics, the tertiary sector is the sector that sells services.
normal.cn: 经济上的 tertiary sector 是指出售服务的部门。

normal.en: Compare secondary: secondary is the middle stage, tertiary is the one after it.
normal.cn: 对比 secondary：secondary 是中间阶段，tertiary 是它之后的阶段。

abstract.en: Picture a stair with the first two steps worn down and your foot coming to rest on the third.
abstract.cn: 想象一级台阶，前两级已被踩旧，你的脚最后落在第三级上。

abstract.en: Imagine three stacked blocks and a small flag planted on the top one.
abstract.cn: 想象三块叠放的积木，最上面那块插着一面小旗。

abstract.en: Think of a race scoreboard with the third lane lighting up.
abstract.cn: 想想一块比赛记分牌，第三条泳道亮了起来。

examples.en: She hopes to go into tertiary education next year.
examples.cn: 她希望明年进入高等教育阶段。

examples.en: The clinic assesses patients who need tertiary care in a specialist unit.
examples.cn: 这家门诊为需要三级专科医疗的病人做评估。

examples.en: The course moves from basic grammar into a tertiary stage of writing.
examples.cn: 这门课从基础语法推进到写作的第三阶段。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「特舍里」——三级台阶「特」别高，「舍」不得停在前两级，只能上到 tertiary 这一级；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 tertius（第三）＋ -arius（属于……的）→ tertiarius（第三等的）→ 英语 tertiary，核心义「排在一二之后的第三个」。

sensesIntro.en: Tertiary is one number word in several numbered systems: schooling, rank, the economy, geology, medicine, and course stages.
sensesIntro.cn: tertiary 是同一类「第三」的数词，散落在几套编号系统里：学制、等级、国民经济、地质、医疗与课程阶段。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a foot reaching the third step of a stair after two earlier ones.
core.cn: 核心意象：走过前两级台阶后，脚落在第三级上。

branches.en: The schooling and course-stage senses both count study in three steps.
branches.cn: 学制义与课程阶段义都按三个台阶来数学习过程。

branches.en: Ranks and levels of care are the plain ordinal sense applied to institutions.
branches.cn: 等级义与医疗等级义都是序数本义用在机构分类上。

branches.en: The economy is counted in three blocks, and the last is services.
branches.cn: 经济被分成三大块，最后一块是服务业。

branches.en: Geology took the same number for a whole era of rock.
branches.cn: 地质学拿同一个数字来命名一整个岩石时代。

branches.en: Both work by ranking a big system in three numbered levels.
branches.cn: 两者都是把一个庞大体系按三个等级来编号。

intro.en: Tertiary is Latin tertius, third, plus the adjective suffix -arius; the family runs through the -ary number words.
intro.cn: tertiary 是拉丁语 tertius（第三）加形容词词尾 -arius；这一词族贯穿各类 -ary 数词形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin tertius means third, and -arius means belonging to, so tertiarius means of the third class.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tertius 意为第三，-arius 意为属于……的，因此 tertiarius 就是「属于第三等」。

items.example: Tertius is the ordinal number three, and it supplies the stem of this word.
items.exampleCN: tertius 是拉丁语序数词「第三」，也是这个词的词干来源。

items.example: The suffix -arius turns a number into a word meaning of that rank or class.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -arius 把一个数词变成表示该等级或类别的形容词。

items.example: Tertiary keeps the -ary shape that Latin -arius gives in English.
items.exampleCN: tertiary 保留了拉丁语 -arius 在英语中化作 -ary 的形态。

items.example: The same stem of three returns in tri- compounds such as triangle.
items.exampleCN: 与「三」同源的词干也出现在 triangle 等 tri- 复合词中。

items.example: Ternary uses the distributive number three rather than the ordinal.
items.exampleCN: ternary 用的是表示「每三个一组」的分配数词，而非序数词。

items.example: Quartus onwards builds quaternary, the word for a fourth order.
items.exampleCN: 从 quartus 起又构成 quaternary，表示第四纪或四层级。

items.meaning: of the fourth rank or order
items.example: Quaternary is the direct sibling of tertiary in a numbered series.
items.exampleCN: quaternary 是一个编号序列中与 tertiary 直接对应的同胞词。

items.meaningCN: 每隔一天发作的；间日热的
items.example: Tertian counts a fever that returns on the third day, the same number image.
items.exampleCN: tertian 指每隔一天发作一次的发热，是同一套「第三天」的计数意象。

items.meaning: coming after the first, not leading
items.example: Secondary shows the ordinary -ary rank word that tertiary answers.
items.exampleCN: secondary 是普通的 -ary 序位词，tertiary 正与它相承。

items.meaningCN: 由拉丁词干构成形容词的词尾
items.example: The ending -ary is the living English form of Latin -arius.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ary 是拉丁语 -arius 在英语中的现役形态。

latinEntries.meaning: of the third, of the third class

definition_zh: 破伤风；强直性痉挛
definition_en: a serious bacterial disease that causes stiffness of the jaw and violent muscle spasms
core_image: 全身肌肉一寸寸绷成一根直棍，连下巴都被锁住，张不开嘴
scene: 园丁的手被生锈的铁丝划破，医生给他打了针，因为泥土里的病菌可能引起这种僵直的病。The gardener cut his hand on a rusty wire fence, so the nurse gave him an injection against tetanus.
sceneCN: 这里 tetanus 是「破伤风」（第 1 个义项：由伤口泥土中细菌引起、肌肉僵直的严重疾病）；句意：园丁的手被生锈的铁丝网划破，所以护士给他打了一针破伤风预防针。

pos.zh: 破伤风；强直性痉挛（不可数名词，医学与日常通用）

forms.label: 同类名词无复数（不可数），复数形仅见于极少数文献
形容词（由 tetanus 加 -ic 构成）

derivatives.zh: 由病名加形容词后缀 -ic 构成，义为「破伤风的；强直性收缩的」
指血钙过低引起的持续肌痉挛，与病名同出希腊语「绷紧」词根
由 tetanic 的词干加动词后缀 -ise 构成，义为「使肌肉强直收缩」

senses.title: The bacterial disease
senses.definition: a serious disease caused by bacteria that enter through a wound and release a toxin making the muscles stiff and shaking
senses.definitionCN: 由伤口进入的细菌释放毒素，使肌肉僵直并阵阵抽搐的严重疾病
senses.example: Doctors warn that tetanus can be fatal within days.
senses.exampleCN: 医生警告说，破伤风可能在几天内致命。
senses.why: The Greek adjective for stretched tight names the disease by the single most visible sign: a body pulled rigid.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语中表示「绷得紧紧的」这个形容词，用最醒目的一个病象给病命名：身体被拉得僵直。

senses.title: The sickness of locked muscles
senses.definition: the older medical sense of any prolonged stiffness or lockjaw, before the cause was known
senses.definitionCN: 在病因尚未弄清之前，泛指一切持续僵直或牙关紧闭的旧医学说法
senses.example: Early physicians used tetanus for any sickness that fixed the neck and jaw.
senses.exampleCN: 早期医生把凡是使颈与颌僵硬固定的病都叫 tetanus。
senses.why: Before bacteria were discovered, the name described the locked posture rather than any germ.
senses.whyCN: 在发现细菌之前，这个名字描绘的是被锁住的身姿，而非某种病菌。

senses.title: A sustained muscle contraction
senses.definition: a state in which a muscle stays contracted instead of alternating between tension and rest
senses.definitionCN: 肌肉持续保持收缩、不在紧张与放松之间交替的状态
senses.example: A sustained tetanus in the calf muscle can be felt as a hard, unyielding knot.
senses.exampleCN: 小腿肌肉的持续强直性收缩，摸上去是一个坚硬不退的硬块。
senses.why: Physiologists borrowed the disease word for the pure state of a muscle that will not let go.
senses.whyCN: 生理学家借用了这个病名，来指肌肉「不肯松开」的纯粹状态。

intro.en: Tetanus comes from Latin tetanus, from Greek tetanos, the medical name for a stretched, rigid spasm, built on teinein, to stretch.
intro.cn: tetanus 来自拉丁语 tetanus，更早是希腊语 tetanos（绷紧僵直的痉挛），源于动词 teinein（拉紧）。

items.en: Teinein means to stretch or to draw something tight.
items.cn: teinein 意为拉伸、把某物抽紧。

items.en: Tetanos means stretched, and names the locked stiffness of a body in spasm.
items.cn: tetanos 意为绷紧的，指痉挛时身体僵直锁住的状态。

items.en: Latin borrows tetanus as the name of that rigid spasm in medical writing.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 tetanus，作为医学书写中这种僵直痉挛的名称。

items.en: English takes tetanus as a learned term for a locked, stiffening illness.
items.cn: 英语借入 tetanus，作为表示僵直疾病的学术用语。

items.en: Bacteriology identifies the soil germ and its toxin, and the name is fixed on the wound disease.
items.cn: 细菌学确认了泥土中的病菌及其毒素，病名从此固定在伤口感染上。

items.en: Tetanus becomes a vaccine-preventable disease, and it also names sustained muscle contraction.
items.cn: 现代英语中破伤风成为可用疫苗预防的疾病，同时也用来指持续的肌肉收缩。

note.en: Group one holds the Greek stretching stem and its medical relatives; group two holds the everyday names and other diseases of locked muscles.
note.cn: 第一组是希腊语「拉紧」词干及其医学同族词；第二组是日常俗称与其它肌肉锁住的病。

entries.definition: of tetanus, or of a sustained contraction
entries.definitionCN: 破伤风的；强直性收缩的

entries.definition: a condition of continuous muscle spasm, often from low calcium
entries.definitionCN: 常由血钙过低引起的持续性肌痉挛

entries.definition: resembling tetanus in stiffness
the everyday name for tetanus, from the locked jaw
entries.definitionCN: 破伤风的旧俗称，字面就是「锁颌」

entries.definition: a viral disease that also brings spasms and fear of water
entries.definitionCN: 同样引起抽搐与恐水的病毒性疾病

entries.definition: a sudden tight contraction of a muscle

normalIntro.en: Tetanus is the Greek word for stretched tight: the disease is named after the locked posture it forces on the body.
normalIntro.cn: tetanus 在希腊语里意为「绷得紧紧的」：这种病就是按它强加给身体的锁死姿态命名的。

normal.en: Greek teinein means to stretch, and tetanos means stretched tight.
normal.cn: 希腊语 teinein 意为拉紧，tetanos 意为绷紧的。

normal.en: The bacterium enters through a dirty wound, so clean and cover every cut.
normal.cn: 病菌经由脏伤口进入，所以任何伤口都要清洗并覆盖。

normal.en: A tetanus vaccine is given regularly to keep protection alive.
normal.cn: 需要定期接种破伤风疫苗以维持保护力。

normal.en: Lockjaw is the old English name for the same disease.
normal.cn: lockjaw 是同一种病的英语旧称。

normal.en: Compare spasm: a spasm is one contraction, tetanus is the whole disease or a locked contraction.
normal.cn: 对比 spasm：spasm 指一次收缩，tetanus 指整种病或持续锁住的收缩。

abstract.en: Picture a jaw screwed shut while the whole body is drawn into a straight line.
abstract.cn: 想象下巴被螺丝拧死，全身又被拉成一条直线。

abstract.en: Imagine a rubber band pulled until it can only quiver and will not relax.
abstract.cn: 想象一根橡皮筋被拉到极限，只会颤抖而无法放松。

abstract.en: Think of a door lock that clicks shut and will not open.
abstract.cn: 想想一把咔哒一声锁死、再也打不开的门锁。

examples.en: The nurse checked when he had last had a tetanus injection.
examples.cn: 护士查问他上一次打破伤风针是什么时候。

examples.en: A deep cut from rusty metal should be checked for tetanus risk.
examples.cn: 被生锈金属划出的深口子要检查破伤风风险。

examples.en: Vaccination has made tetanus rare in many countries.
examples.cn: 在许多国家，接种疫苗已使破伤风变得少见。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「贴他得死」——一身肌肉贴得铁硬、僵直不动，病重时真的会要命，所以 tetanus 是破伤风；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 teinein（拉紧）→ tetanos（绷紧的；僵直痉挛）→ 拉丁语 tetanus → 英语 tetanus，核心义「身体被绷紧锁死」。

sensesIntro.en: Tetanus first names the wound disease, then the old picture of any locked illness, and finally the muscle state of staying contracted.
sensesIntro.cn: tetanus 先指伤口感染的这种病，再指旧式的「锁紧型疾病」病象，最后指肌肉持续收缩的生理状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body stretched rigid, with the jaw locked shut.
core.cn: 核心意象：身体被绷成硬棍，下巴被锁死。

branches.en: The germ disease and the old locked-illness sense both describe the same rigid body.
branches.cn: 病菌引起的病与旧式的「锁紧型疾病」描绘的是同一具僵直的身体。

branches.en: The name also lives on for any muscle that stays contracted.
branches.cn: 这个名字也留存下来，指任何持续保持收缩的肌肉。

branches.en: Both are about a body held in a fixed posture, not about a germ.
branches.cn: 两者都讲身体被固定在一个姿势里，而不是讲细菌。

branches.en: The wound disease is the everyday reason the word is met today.
branches.cn: 伤口感染的病是今天遇到这个词最常见的理由。

branches.en: A tetanic contraction in the clinic carries the same name as the illness.
branches.cn: 临床上强直性收缩与那种病共用同一个名字。

intro.en: Tetanus is a Greek medical noun kept in Latin form, with tetanic, tetany, and lockjaw built around the stretched-tight image.
intro.cn: tetanus 是以拉丁形式保留的希腊语医学名词，围绕「绷紧」这一意象又派生出 tetanic、tetany 与 lockjaw。

latinIntro.en: Greek teinein means to stretch and tetanos means stretched; Latin tetanus keeps the noun for the rigid spasm.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 teinein 意为拉紧，tetanos 意为绷紧的；拉丁语 tetanus 保留了表示僵直痉挛的名词。

items.example: Tetanos describes a body or a limb pulled stiff and held rigid.
items.exampleCN: tetanos 形容身体或肢体被绷得笔直、僵硬。

items.example: Teinein is the stretching verb behind the stiff name.
items.exampleCN: teinein 是这股「拉紧」意象背后的动词。

items.meaning: the disease of rigid, locked muscles
items.meaningCN: 肌肉僵硬、牙关紧闭的疾病
items.example: Tetanus keeps the Greek image of a body stretched stiff.
items.exampleCN: tetanus 保留了希腊语里身体被绷成一根直棍的画面。

items.example: The ending -us marks the Latin and Greek masculine noun.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -us 标示拉丁语与希腊语的阳性名词。

items.meaning: of tetanus, or of a sustained contraction
items.meaningCN: 破伤风的；强直性收缩的
items.example: The adjective tetanic modifies symptoms such as a tetanic spasm.
items.exampleCN: 形容词 tetanic 修饰 tetanic spasm 这类症状。

items.example: The suffix -ic turns the disease name into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ic 把病名变成形容词。

items.meaning: the poison made by the bacterium
items.example: Tetanus toxin is the substance that locks the muscles.
items.exampleCN: tetanus toxin 就是让肌肉锁死的物质。

items.example: The ending -in, as in toxin, names a substance.
items.exampleCN: toxin 里的 -in 用来给一种物质命名。

items.meaning: the old everyday name for tetanus
items.example: Lockjaw paints the same condition as a locked jaw.
items.exampleCN: lockjaw 用「锁住的颌」描绘同一种病象。

items.example: Antitetanus describes a serum or an injection given against the disease.
items.exampleCN: antitetanus 指用来对抗这种病的血清或注射剂。

definition_zh: 理论家；理论工作者；学说提出者
definition_en: a person who develops the ideas and principles behind a subject rather than only practising it
core_image: 一个人坐在窗边看整盘棋，不落一子，却把每一步的理由写在纸上
scene: 学术会议上，做实验的同事把数据摊在桌上，而那位只写模型的人只管追问背后的原理。At the conference the experimental colleague spread out the data while the theorist kept asking what principle explained it.
sceneCN: 这里的 theorist 是「理论家」（第 1 个义项：以提出和整理理论为主要工作的人）；句意：会议上，做实验的同事摊开数据，而那位理论家却不停追问哪条原理能解释这些结果。

pos.zh: 理论家；理论工作者；学说提出者

derivatives.zh: 由希腊语 theoria 直接借入，义为「理论；学说」，是 theorist 的基础名词
由 theorist 的同根词干加形容词后缀 -ical 构成，义为「理论的；理论上的」
由同根词干加动词后缀 -ise 构成，义为「提出理论；进行理论化」

senses.title: A builder of theories
senses.definition: a person who constructs and defends the general ideas that explain a subject
senses.definitionCN: 建立并论证某一领域总体原理与思想的人
senses.example: As a theorist, she is happier with models than with lab equipment.
senses.exampleCN: 作为理论家，她更喜欢模型而不是实验室设备。
senses.why: Greek theoria first meant watching, so the theorist is the one who sees the pattern before anyone acts.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 theoria 起初意为观看，所以理论家是最先看出规律、再有人行动的那个人。

senses.title: A student of abstract ideas
senses.definition: a scholar whose work is abstract thought rather than experiment or practice
senses.definitionCN: 以抽象思考而非实验或实务为工作的学者
senses.example: The panel brought together a theorist and two field researchers.
senses.exampleCN: 这个专家组把一位理论工作者和两位实地研究者聚到了一起。
senses.why: The -ist suffix marks the practiser of a discipline, and here the discipline is abstract thought itself.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -ist 表示从业者，这里的「业」就是抽象思考本身。

senses.title: A holder of an explanation
senses.definition: a person who puts forward a particular explanation of how something happened
senses.definitionCN: 提出关于某事如何发生的某种说法的人
senses.example: Some theorists believe the site was abandoned because of drought.
senses.exampleCN: 一些持此说者认为该遗址是因干旱而被废弃的。
senses.why: A theory can also be one specific explanation, so its supporter is named by the same person word.
senses.whyCN: theory 也可以指某一条具体解释，支持这条解释的人仍用同一个表示人的词来称说。

senses.title: An advocate of a doctrine
senses.definition: a person identified with a school of thought or an ideology
senses.definitionCN: 归属于某一思想流派或意识形态的人
senses.example: She is best known as a theorist of free markets.
senses.exampleCN: 她最为人所知的身份是自由市场学说的倡导者。
senses.why: Once a body of ideas grows into a school, the theorist becomes the public name for that school.
senses.whyCN: 一套思想一旦长成学派，理论家就成了这一学派对外的名字。

senses.title: A supporter of a grand claim
senses.titleCN: 阴谋论者一类的「理论家」
senses.definition: a person who publicly supports an unproven claim, as in the phrase for conspiracy believers
senses.definitionCN: 公开支持未经证实说法的人，如 conspiracy theorist 这一说法中
senses.example: The phrase for a conspiracy believer places a theorist at the end.
senses.exampleCN: 指阴谋论信奉者的那个说法，把 theorist 放在最后。
senses.why: Fixed phrases can stretch the person word beyond scholarship until it merely labels a claimant.
senses.whyCN: 固定短语会把这个人称名词用出学术之外，最后只剩「主张者」这一层标签义。

intro.en: Theorist joins theory, from Greek theoria, a looking at or contemplation, to the person suffix -ist.
intro.cn: theorist 由 theory（源自希腊语 theoria，观看、静观）加表示人的词尾 -ist 构成。

items.en: Theorein means to look at or to contemplate, and theoria means a beholding.
items.cn: theorein 意为观看、沉思，theoria 意为观看、静观。

items.en: A theoros was a spectator, including a citizen sent to watch sacred games.
items.cn: theoros 指观者，其中包括被派去观看宗教竞技的公民。

items.en: Late Latin theoria takes the word over for contemplation and study.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 theoria 把这个词接下，用来指静观与研究。

items.en: Theory enters English for a kind of viewing of truth, first in church and learned writing.
items.cn: theory 进入英语时指对真理的一种观照，初见于教会与学术文字。

items.en: The person suffix -ist is attached, and theorist appears for one given to speculation.
items.cn: 表示人的词尾 -ist 加上去，theorist 出现，指耽于思辨的人。

items.en: Theorist settles on the scholar or thinker who builds and tests general ideas.
items.cn: 现代英语中 theorist 固定在建立并检验总体思想体系的学者身上。

note.en: Group one holds the Greek looking stem and its English family; group two holds other words for people who think or build ideas.
note.cn: 第一组是希腊语「观看」词干及其英语词族；第二组是其它表示思考者或提出思想之人的词。

entries.definition: a system of ideas used to explain something
entries.definitionCN: 用来解释某事的观念体系

entries.definition: based on ideas rather than practice
to form theories
a person who thinks deeply about matters
a person who studies fundamental questions
entries.definitionCN: 研究根本问题的哲学家

entries.definition: a person who gathers evidence for a study

normalIntro.en: Theorist is theory plus -ist, a person suffix, so the word always points at the human builder of ideas.
normalIntro.cn: theorist 就是 theory 加表示人的词尾 -ist，所以这个词总指向提出思想的那个人。

normal.en: Theory is the thought system, theorist is the person who builds it.
normal.cn: theory 是思想体系，theorist 是建立它的那个人。

normal.en: The same pair pattern appears in economy and economist.
normal.cn: 同一对构词规律也出现在 economy 与 economist 上。

normal.en: Greek theoria means watching, from the spectator in the stands.
normal.cn: 希腊语 theoria 意为观看，源自看台上的观者。

normal.en: In academic writing, a theorist offers models and general claims.
normal.cn: 在学术写作里，theorist 提供模型与一般性主张。

normal.en: Conspiracy theorist shows that the word can also mark a supporter of an unproven claim.
normal.cn: conspiracy theorist 显示这个词也能指某种未经证实说法的支持者。

abstract.en: Picture someone viewing a whole chessboard while the pieces stay in their hands.
abstract.cn: 想象有人端看整盘棋，棋子却一直捏在手里没落下。

abstract.en: Imagine a closed notebook on a desk, its pages full of arrows.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上摊着一本合拢的笔记，页面上尽是箭头。

abstract.en: Think of a map drawn first by a geographer who never left the room.
abstract.cn: 想想一位从未离开房间的地理学者先画出的那张地图。

examples.en: The theorist argued that markets correct themselves.
examples.cn: 这位理论家主张市场会自行回调。

examples.en: Senior theorists in the field disagree about the cause.
examples.cn: 该领域的资深理论家对成因看法不一。

examples.en: A careful theorist builds models that fieldwork can test.
examples.cn: 严谨的理论家会建立可被实地调查检验的模型。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「师理思」——老师专心于「理」与「思」，把道理想通、讲清，这样的人才叫 theorist；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 theorein（观看、沉思）→ theoria（静观）→ 晚期拉丁语 theoria → 英语 theory → 加 -ist（表示人的词尾）→ theorist，核心义「观看并思考原理的人」。

sensesIntro.en: Theorist begins as the builder of abstract ideas, then names a kind of scholar, then the holder of a giving explanation, then a school advocate, and finally an unproven-claim supporter.
sensesIntro.cn: theorist 先指抽象思想的建立者，再指一类学者，再指某种解释的提出者，再到学派倡导者，最后指未经证实说法的支持者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spectator who watches the whole game and writes down the reasons.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人旁观整盘比赛，再把其中的道理写下来。

branches.en: Both name a scholar whose work is abstract thought itself.
branches.cn: 两者都指以抽象思考本身为工作的学者。

branches.en: Both narrow from thought in general to a particular explanation or school.
branches.cn: 两者都从一般思想收窄到某种具体解释或学派。

branches.en: The unproven-claim use turns the word into a label in a fixed phrase.
branches.cn: 「无据说法支持者」这一用法把词固定在一个短语里当标签用。

branches.en: A builder of theory can also be the representative voice of a school.
branches.cn: 理论建立者也常是某个学说流派的代表声音。

branches.en: Both separate the thinking person from the practitioner or the evidence.
branches.cn: 两者都把思考的人与实践者、与证据分开。

intro.en: Theorist is the Greek looking stem seen in theory and theorem, plus the person suffix -ist that marks the practiser.
intro.cn: theorist 由 theory、theorem 中可见的希腊语「观看」词干，加上标示「从事者」的人称词尾 -ist 构成。

latinIntro.en: Greek theoria means a beholding, which Late Latin keeps for contemplation; the person suffix -ist came on later in English and French.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 theoria 意为静观，晚期拉丁语沿用其「沉思」之义；表示人的 -ist 则较晚经法语进入英语。

items.example: Theoria begins as the act of looking at something rather than doing it.
items.exampleCN: theoria 起初指「看」这件事本身，而非动手去做。

items.meaning: a spectator sent to look on
items.example: The theoros was the spectator, the person sent to watch.
items.exampleCN: theoros 就是观者，被派去观看的人。

items.example: Theorein supplies the stem of theory and theorist alike.
items.exampleCN: theorein 同时提供了 theory 与 theorist 的词干。

items.meaning: a system of ideas, or contemplation
items.example: Theory is the noun of looking and knowing that theorist presupposes.
items.exampleCN: theory 是 theorist 所依托的那个「观看与认识」的名词。

items.example: Theoretical shows the -etic form of the same Greek stem.
items.exampleCN: theoretical 展示了同一希腊词干的 -etic 形态。

items.example: Theorise is the verb, and he who theorises is a theorist.
items.exampleCN: theorise 是动词，而 theorise 的人就是 theorist。

items.meaningCN: 从事某活动的人（名词词尾）
items.example: The person suffix -ist marks the agent behind theory.
items.exampleCN: 表示人的词尾 -ist 标出 theory 背后的施动者。

items.example: Theorist joins the concept and its maker in one word.
items.exampleCN: theorist 把一门理论与其建立者合于一词。

items.example: The same pattern gives economist and novelist.
items.exampleCN: 同样的构词式也造就了 economist 与 novelist。

items.meaning: of a theorist or of theorising
items.example: Theoristic marks the rare adjective built on the person word.
items.exampleCN: theoristic 是基于这个人称名词的罕见形容词。

definition_zh: 治疗师；理疗师；心理治疗师；咨询师
definition_en: a trained person who treats physical or mental problems, often with methods other than medicine
core_image: 一双手扶住正在康复的人，耐心地一步步领着对方走
scene: 心理咨询室的门轻轻关上，访客坐在沙发里低头沉默。The therapist waited quietly, then asked how the week had gone.
sceneCN: 这里 therapist 是「心理治疗师」（第 1 个义项：受过训练、以谈话或手法帮助人恢复的人）；句意为治疗师安静等着，然后问访客这一周过得怎样。

pos.zh: 治疗师；理疗师；心理治疗师

derivatives.zh: 由希腊语词根 therapy 直接构成，义为「治疗；疗法」
加形容词后缀 -ic，义为「治疗的；有疗效的」
再加副词后缀 -ally，义为「以治疗的方式」
前缀 psycho-（心理）加本词，义为「心理治疗师」

senses.title: A person trained to treat illness
senses.definition: a trained professional who treats physical or mental problems with methods such as exercise, massage or talking
senses.definitionCN: 受过训练、用手法、运动或谈话等方式治疗身体或心理问题的专业人员
senses.example: The therapist taught her exercises to strengthen her knee.
senses.exampleCN: 治疗师教她做了几组强化膝盖的练习。
senses.why: The Greek root therapeuein means to attend or heal, so a therapist is the person who does the healing work.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语词根意为「照料、医治」，所以治疗师就是动手做医治工作的人。

senses.title: A specialist in talking about feelings
senses.titleCN: 心理治疗师；心理咨询师
senses.definition: a professional who helps people with emotional or mental difficulties mainly through conversation
senses.definitionCN: 主要通过交谈帮助人处理情绪或心理困扰的专业人士
senses.example: After the accident he began seeing a therapist every week.
senses.exampleCN: 事故之后，他开始每周去看一次心理治疗师。
senses.why: When healing moved from the body to the mind, the same word came to name the listener in the chair.
senses.whyCN: 当医治的对象从身体转向内心，同一个词就用来指坐在椅子对面倾听的人。

senses.title: A helper attached to a specific service
senses.definition: a worker whose title names the service they provide, such as speech or occupational therapy
senses.definitionCN: 头衔里标明所提供服务的从业人员，如言语治疗师或职业治疗师
senses.example: A speech therapist worked with the boy on his stammer.
senses.exampleCN: 一位言语治疗师帮助那个男孩纠正口吃。
senses.why: Therapist became a building block, so any front word names the kind of healing that person offers.
senses.whyCN: therapist 后来变成了构词部件，前面加什么词，就说明这个人提供哪一类治疗。

intro.en: Therapist is built on the Greek root for healing or attending, therapeuein, and the agent ending -ist.
intro.cn: therapist 由希腊语表示「医治、照料」的词根 therapeuein 加上表示「人」的后缀 -ist 构成。

items.en: Therapeuein means to serve, attend to or treat, and therapeia means service or care.
items.cn: therapeuein 意为服务、照料或医治，therapeia 意为服务、护理。

items.en: Medieval Latin therapy and therapeuta carry the Greek word into European use.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 therapy 与 therapeuta 把希腊词带入欧洲。

items.en: Therapy first names the medical treatment of disease in English.
items.cn: therapy 在英语中最初指对疾病的医学治疗。

items.en: The word therapist appears as a name for a medical healer.
items.cn: therapist 出现，用作对医者的称呼。

items.en: Psychotherapy gives the short form therapist its strong mental health sense.
items.cn: 心理治疗的发展让 therapist 这一简称获得了强烈的心理健康含义。

note.en: Therapist belongs to the therapy family, and sits close to doctor, psychologist and counsellor.
note.cn: therapist 属于 therapy 词族，与 doctor、psychologist、counsellor 相邻。

entries.definition: the treatment of an illness or a mental difficulty
connected with the treatment of illness
a therapist who treats the body with movement and massage
entries.definitionCN: 以运动和按摩治疗身体问题的治疗师

entries.definition: a specialist who studies and treats the mind
a person trained to give advice and support
a doctor of medicine

normalIntro.en: Therapist is therapy plus the person ending: the one who gives the therapy.
normalIntro.cn: therapist 就是 therapy 加上表示「人」的后缀：提供治疗的那位。

normal.en: The ending -ist marks a person, as in artist and scientist.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ist 标记一个人，如 artist 与 scientist。

normal.en: Therapy is the treatment, so the therapist is the one who treats.
normal.cn: therapy 是治疗本身，所以 therapist 是实施治疗的人。

normal.en: Physical therapist, speech therapist and occupational therapist name the field before the word.
normal.cn: physical、speech、occupational 放在词前，说明治疗的具体领域。

normal.en: To see a therapist is the usual way to say you get talking therapy.
normal.cn: see a therapist 是表示去做心理谈话治疗的常用说法。

normal.en: Compare therapist and psychiatrist: the second can prescribe drugs, the first usually cannot.
normal.cn: 对比 psychiatrist：后者可以开药，而 therapist 通常不能。

abstract.en: Picture two hands guiding a patient along parallel bars.
abstract.cn: 想象一双手扶着病人沿平行杆往前走。

abstract.en: Imagine a quiet room with two chairs facing each other.
abstract.cn: 想象一间安静的房间，两把椅子面对面。

abstract.en: See a label on a clinic door naming the special care inside.
abstract.cn: 想象诊所门上一块牌子，写着里面提供的专门照护。

examples.en: The therapist helped him walk again after the surgery.
examples.cn: 手术后那位治疗师帮助他重新走路。

examples.en: She has been seeing a therapist since she lost her job.
examples.cn: 她失业后一直在看心理治疗师。

examples.en: Our clinic now employs two physical therapists.
examples.cn: 我们的诊所现在聘用两名物理治疗师。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「塞拉皮斯特」——塞给病人拉一把的理疗师；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 therapeuein（服侍、照料、医治）→ 拉丁语 therapeuta → 英语 therapy + -ist → therapist，核心义「照护并医治他人的人」。

sensesIntro.en: Therapist starts as a general healer, then narrows to the mental health listener, and finally serves as a building block in compound titles.
sensesIntro.cn: therapist 先指一般的医治者，再收窄到心理领域的倾听者，最后成为复合头衔中的构词部件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands steadying a recovering patient.
core.cn: 核心意象：一双手扶住正在康复的病人。

branches.en: The general healer sense keeps the body in view.
branches.cn: 一般的医治者义项仍以身体为对象。

branches.en: The talking sense moves healing into the mind.
branches.cn: 谈话义项把医治挪到了内心。

branches.en: The compound title sense turns the word into a label.
branches.cn: 复合头衔义项把词变成了标签。

branches.en: Both senses name a trained worker who offers a service.
branches.cn: 两个义项都指受过训练、提供某项服务的从业者。

branches.en: A speech therapist and a psychotherapist both carry the healing name.
branches.cn: 言语治疗师与心理治疗师都带着「医治」的名称。

intro.en: Therapist is a Greek healing root plus the person suffix -ist, and it feeds a large therapy family.
intro.cn: therapist 由希腊语「医治」词根加表示「人」的后缀 -ist 构成，并延伸出庞大的 therapy 词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin took the Greek healing words as therapeuta and therapia, passing them into modern European languages.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语借入希腊语医治词，形成 therapeuta 与 therapia，再传给现代欧洲语言。

items.example: The word comes from therapeuein.
items.exampleCN: 这个词来自 therapeuein。

items.example: Therapeia is the noun behind therapy.
items.exampleCN: therapeia 是 therapy 背后的名词。

items.example: The suffix -ist turns therapy into therapist.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ist 把 therapy 变成 therapist。

items.example: Therapy names the treatment itself.
items.exampleCN: therapy 指治疗本身。

items.example: Therapist adds the person meaning.
items.exampleCN: therapist 加上了「人」的含义。

items.example: The suffix -ic forms therapeutic.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ic 构成 therapeutic。

items.example: The prefix psycho- forms psychotherapist.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 psycho- 构成 psychotherapist。

items.example: The prefix physio- marks treatment of the body.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 physio- 标记身体治疗。

items.example: Speech combines with therapist in speech therapist.
items.exampleCN: speech 与 therapist 组合成言语治疗师。

definition_zh: 演员；（戏剧）表演者；戏剧的；演戏的
definition_en: an actor, especially on the stage, or relating to acting and the theatre
core_image: 一个人戴上面具，走上木板舞台，把别人的命运演给自己看
scene: 幕布升起，聚光灯落在台中央，一个年轻人第一次独自面对满场观众。The young thespian forgot every line and simply stood there in the light.
sceneCN: 这里 thespian 是「演员」（第 1 个义项：在舞台上表演的人，略带正式或诙谐色彩）；句意为这位年轻演员忘了所有台词，只是站在灯光里。

derivatives.zh: 词的本源是人名，义为「据传古希腊第一位悲剧演员」
加名词后缀 -ism，义为「戏剧表演；演戏的风范」

senses.title: An actor, especially on stage
senses.definition: a person who acts in plays, especially one performing on the stage
senses.definitionCN: 在戏剧中表演的人，尤指在舞台上演出的演员
senses.example: The festival brings hundreds of thespians to the small town each summer.
senses.exampleCN: 每年夏天，这个戏剧节都会把数百名演员带到这座小镇。
senses.why: The name of the Greek father of tragedy, Thespis, was turned into a polite word for anyone who acts.
senses.whyCN: 希腊悲剧之父忒斯比斯的名字被借来表示「演戏的人」，成了一种体面的说法。

senses.title: A self-important stage performer
senses.titleCN: （带调侃意味的）戏骨；爱演的人
senses.definition: an actor, often used with gentle humour for someone who loves the stage or overacts
senses.definitionCN: 演员，常带轻松调侃的意味，指热爱舞台或表演夸张的人
senses.example: He is a true thespian, forever quoting lines at the dinner table.
senses.exampleCN: 他是个十足的爱演之人，吃饭时也不停背台词。
senses.why: Because the word is old and formal, saying it with a smile gently mocks stagey behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 正因为这个词古老又正式，笑着说出来就带上了对「舞台腔」的善意戏谑。

senses.title: Relating to the theatre
senses.definition: connected with acting, drama or the theatre, used as an adjective
senses.definitionCN: 作形容词，指与表演、戏剧或剧场有关的
senses.example: Critics praised his thespian gifts long before he entered film.
senses.exampleCN: 早在他进入电影圈之前，评论界就称赞他的演戏天赋。
senses.why: From the noun came an adjective meaning belonging to the stage, used in phrases such as thespian art.
senses.whyCN: 由名词又长出形容词，意为「属于舞台的」，形成了 thespian art 这类说法。

intro.en: Thespian comes from Thespis, the legendary first actor of Greek tragedy, through the adjective for the town Thespiae.
intro.cn: thespian 来自希腊悲剧传说中第一位演员忒斯比斯，经由指其故乡忒斯比阿镇的形容词传入英语。

items.en: Thespis is remembered in tradition as the first actor to step out of the chorus.
items.cn: 传统上把忒斯比斯记为第一位从歌队中走出单独表演的演员。

items.en: Thespiai is the town in Boeotia linked with his name.
items.cn: 忒斯比阿是与他名字相连的希腊城镇。

items.en: Latin Thespius and Thespiades connect the name with the stage.
items.cn: 拉丁语 Thespius 与 Thespiades 把这一名字与舞台联系起来。

items.en: Thespian appears in English as an adjective for the stage and for tragic poetry.
items.cn: thespian 以形容词形式进入英语，指舞台的或悲剧诗歌的。

items.en: Thespian settles as a slightly grand or jocular word for an actor.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，thespian 固定为对演员稍微郑重或诙谐的称呼。

note.en: Thespian has no true root family beyond the name Thespis, so it sits next to acting words and to stage, drama and theatre terms.
note.cn: thespian 除人名忒斯比斯外没有真正的同根词，因此与表演词及 stage、drama、theatre 一类用语相邻。

entries.definition: the legendary first actor of Greek tragedy
entries.definitionCN: 传说中希腊悲剧的第一位演员

entries.definition: the practice or style of acting
the drama or the building where plays are staged
a person who performs in plays or films
a person who entertains an audience
a writer of plays

normalIntro.en: Thespian carries the name of Thespis, so the spelling keeps the th and the -ian adjective ending.
normalIntro.cn: thespian 带着忒斯比斯的名字，所以保留 th 开头和 -ian 形容词词尾。

normal.en: The twin letters th at the start are the Greek sound, as in theatre and theme.
normal.cn: 开头的 th 是希腊词常见的发音，与 theatre、theme 一样。

normal.en: The ending -ian is an adjective ending seen in Victorian and Christian.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ian 是常见的形容词词尾，如 Victorian、Christian。

normal.en: Thespian is a formal or playful way to say actor, as in a young thespian.
normal.cn: thespian 是 actor 的正式或俏皮说法，如 a young thespian。

normal.en: The adjective use appears in thespian art and thespian talents.
normal.cn: 形容词用法见于 thespian art 与 thespian talents。

normal.en: Do not confuse thespian with thespianism, the noun for the craft of acting.
normal.cn: 不要混淆 thespian 与 thespianism，后者是表示「表演这一行」的名词。

abstract.en: Picture a single actor stepping out of a chorus of masks.
abstract.cn: 想象一个演员从戴面具的歌队中走出。

abstract.en: Imagine someone reciting a speech at a dinner table, fork in hand.
abstract.cn: 想象有人一手拿叉，在饭桌上朗诵台词。

abstract.en: See a spotlight finding a performer at centre stage.
abstract.cn: 想象一束聚光灯落在台中央的表演者身上。

examples.en: Several thespians from the local theatre joined the parade.
examples.cn: 本地剧院的几位演员参加了游行。

examples.en: My uncle was a noted thespian in his younger days.
examples.cn: 我叔叔年轻时是位颇有名气的演员。

examples.en: They performed a thespian version of the old village story.
examples.cn: 他们把那个古老的村庄故事演成了戏剧版本。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死皮安」——演员在台上厚着脸皮演到稳当；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古希腊人名 Thespis（传说中第一位悲剧演员）→ 希腊地名 Thespiai 相关形容词 → 拉丁语 Thespius → 英语 thespian，核心义「舞台上的表演者」。

sensesIntro.en: Thespian names an actor, then lends itself to humorous or affectionate use, and finally works as an adjective for anything theatrical.
sensesIntro.cn: thespian 先指演员，再被用于诙谐或亲昵的称呼，最后作形容词表示「与戏剧有关」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a performer in a mask under a stage light.
core.cn: 核心意象：舞台灯下戴面具的表演者。

branches.en: The everyday sense names a stage actor.
branches.cn: 日常义项指舞台演员。

branches.en: The playful sense colours the word with affection or irony.
branches.cn: 调侃义项给词染上亲昵或反讽的色彩。

branches.en: The adjective sense opens out to drama in general.
branches.cn: 形容词义项把词义扩展到整个戏剧领域。

branches.en: Both noun senses point to a person who loves to perform.
branches.cn: 两个名词义项都指向热爱表演的人。

branches.en: The actor and the adjective both come from the stage and its craft.
branches.cn: 演员义项与形容词义项都源自舞台及其技艺。

intro.en: Thespian is built on a proper name plus the adjective ending -ian, with a small family of theatrical words around it.
intro.cn: thespian 由人名加上形容词词尾 -ian 构成，周围是一小族与戏剧有关的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin Thespius and the plural noun Thespiades transmitted the Greek name into European languages.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 Thespius 与复数名词 Thespiades 把希腊人名传给了欧洲语言。

items.meaningCN: 传说中第一位悲剧演员
items.example: Thespis is the root name.
items.exampleCN: 忒斯比斯是词源人名。

items.meaningCN: 与忒斯比斯相连的城镇
items.example: Thespiai gave an adjective form.
items.exampleCN: 忒斯比阿镇给出了形容词形式。

items.example: The suffix -ian forms thespian.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ian 构成 thespian。

items.example: The shorter -an does the same work in Roman.
items.exampleCN: 更短的 -an 在 Roman 中起同样作用。

items.example: The suffix -ism forms thespianism.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ism 构成 thespianism。

items.example: Actor is the plain everyday word.
items.exampleCN: actor 是日常的普通说法。

items.example: Actress shares the acting root.
items.exampleCN: actress 共享「表演」词根。

items.example: Theatre shares the Greek th sound.
items.exampleCN: theatre 共享希腊词常见的 th 发音。

items.meaning: a play or the art of plays
items.example: Drama names the art itself.
items.exampleCN: drama 指戏剧艺术本身。

definition_zh: 大腿；股；（动物或衣物的）大腿部位
definition_en: the part of the leg between the hip and the knee, or the matching part in an animal or garment
core_image: 一条从髋骨延伸到膝盖的厚实柱体，撑起整个人站立的重量
scene: 跑完长坡之后，运动员扶着栏杆停下来，手按在发热的腿上部。A sharp pain shot through his thigh with every step.
sceneCN: 这里 thigh 是「大腿」（第 1 个义项：髋部到膝盖之间的人体部位）；句意为每一步都有一阵剧痛穿过他的大腿。

derivatives.zh: 复数复合名词，thigh 加 bone，义为「股骨」
形容词复合词，thigh 加 high，义为「及大腿的」
口语复合词，指让人笑得拍大腿的笑话

senses.title: The upper part of the human leg
senses.definition: the thick part of the human leg between the hip and the knee
senses.definitionCN: 人体腿部从髋部到膝盖之间的粗壮部分
senses.example: She pulled a muscle in her left thigh while climbing.
senses.exampleCN: 她攀爬时拉伤了左大腿的肌肉。
senses.why: The Old English word named exactly this section of the body, the thick upper leg, and that picture still leads every use.
senses.whyCN: 古英语这个词本来就是指身体上这一段粗壮的腿上部，这个画面至今仍是所有用法的起点。

senses.title: The matching part in an animal
senses.definition: the same upper leg part in an animal, often eaten as meat such as a chicken thigh
senses.definitionCN: 动物身上相应的腿上部，常作为肉食用，如鸡腿
senses.example: Marinate the chicken thighs in lemon and herbs before grilling.
senses.exampleCN: 烤之前先把鸡腿用柠檬和香草腌好。
senses.why: People mapped the human body part onto animals, and butchers kept the same word for that cut of meat.
senses.whyCN: 人们把人体部位映射到动物身上，肉贩也就用同一个词称呼那一块肉。

senses.title: The matching part of a garment
senses.definition: the part of a piece of clothing, especially trousers, that covers the upper leg
senses.definitionCN: 衣物尤其是裤子覆盖腿上部的那一部分
senses.example: He patched the worn thigh of his work trousers.
senses.exampleCN: 他给工装裤磨破的大腿部位打了补丁。
senses.why: Clothing follows the body it covers, so the covering gained the body part name.
senses.whyCN: 衣物是照着身体剪裁的，于是覆盖腿部的那一块也顺手借了身体部位的名称。

intro.en: Thigh is a native Old English word, recorded as theu in early texts, with relatives in older Germanic languages.
intro.cn: thigh 是古英语本族词，早期文献写作 theu，在更早的日耳曼语中也有同源形式。

items.en: A form usually reconstructed as theuham is thought to mean the thigh or a muscle.
items.cn: 一般把重构形式 theuham 理解为大腿或肌肉。

items.en: The word appears as theu, meaning the thigh or the upper leg.
items.cn: 古英语写作 theu，意为大腿或腿上部。

items.en: Spelling settles towards thigh with the final fricative sound.
items.cn: 到中古英语，拼写逐渐固定为 thigh，末尾保留摩擦音。

items.en: Older forms in other Germanic languages support the same body part meaning.
items.cn: 其他日耳曼语言的早期形式也支持同一身体部位的含义。

items.en: The word extends to animal cuts of meat and to trousers and hose.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个词扩展到动物的肉块以及裤子和长袜。

note.en: Thigh is a body part word, close in spelling to things, and next to leg, knee and haunch.
note.cn: thigh 是身体部位词，拼写上容易与 thin 一类词混淆，意义上与 leg、knee、haunch 相邻。

entries.definition: an object or matter
entries.definitionCN: 东西；事情（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: not thick
entries.definitionCN: 薄的；瘦的（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: far above the ground
entries.definitionCN: 高的（只是读音相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: the whole limb from hip to foot
entries.definitionCN: 腿（从髋到脚的整条肢体）

entries.definition: the joint in the middle of the leg
the hip and upper leg of a person or animal

normalIntro.en: Thigh is a short native word whose gh is silent, so it rhymes with high and sigh.
normalIntro.cn: thigh 是简短的本族词，其中 gh 不发音，因此与 high、sigh 押韵。

normal.en: The gh in thigh is silent, so the vowel sounds like eye.
normal.cn: thigh 里的 gh 不发音，元音读起来像 eye。

normal.en: Add -s for the plural thighs, as in both thighs.
normal.cn: 加 -s 得到复数 thighs，如 both thighs。

normal.en: Thigh combines with bone in thigh bone, the long bone of the upper leg.
normal.cn: thigh 与 bone 组合成 thigh bone，即腿上部那根长骨。

normal.en: On menus, a chicken thigh is the upper leg cut with dark meat.
normal.cn: 在菜单上，chicken thigh 指带深色肉的大腿部位。

normal.en: Compare thigh with calf: the thigh is above the knee, the calf below it.
normal.cn: 对比 calf：大腿在膝盖以上，小腿肚在膝盖以下。

abstract.en: Picture a runner grabbing the top of his leg after a sprint.
abstract.cn: 想象一名跑者冲刺后抓住自己腿上部。

abstract.en: See a plump chicken thigh browning on a grill.
abstract.cn: 想象一只饱满的鸡腿在烤架上烤出焦色。

abstract.en: Imagine a patch sewn onto the thigh of a pair of trousers.
abstract.cn: 想象一条裤子的大腿处缝着一块补丁。

examples.en: The injury kept him off his feet, as his thigh was badly torn.
examples.cn: 伤势让他无法下地，因为他的大腿严重撕裂。

examples.en: Fashion that season called for skirts ending above the thigh.
examples.cn: 那个季节的时尚要求裙子长度不低于大腿。

examples.en: The physiotherapist showed her stretches for the thigh muscles.
examples.cn: 理疗师给她示范了大腿肌肉的拉伸动作。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读起来像「赛」——赛跑时最先发力撑住身体的，就是大腿；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 theu（大腿、腿上部）→ 中古英语 thigh → 现代英语 thigh，并扩展指动物的腿肉与衣物的相应部位。

sensesIntro.en: Thigh begins as a human body part, then spreads to animals and meat, and finally to the clothing that covers it.
sensesIntro.cn: thigh 从人体部位出发，扩展到家畜与肉块，最后又延伸到覆盖该部位的衣物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the thick pillar of the leg above the knee.
core.cn: 核心意象：膝盖以上支撑身体的粗壮柱体。

branches.en: The human body part is the base sense.
branches.cn: 人体部位是最基础的义项。

branches.en: The animal and meat sense maps the body part onto food.
branches.cn: 动物与肉块义项把身体部位映射到食物上。

branches.en: The garment sense follows the body it covers.
branches.cn: 衣物义项跟着它所覆盖的身体走。

branches.en: Human and animal thighs share the same thick upper leg shape.
branches.cn: 人与动物的大腿共享同一种粗壮腿上部形状。

branches.en: A trouser thigh is named for the body part underneath it.
branches.cn: 裤子的大腿部位得名于它下面的身体部位。

intro.en: Thigh is a simple Germanic word with no prefix or suffix of its own, and its short forms come from compounding.
intro.cn: thigh 是简单的日耳曼语词，本身没有前后缀，它的复合形式都来自构词组合。

latinIntro.en: Thigh is not a Latin word; the Latin names for the same body part are femur and coxa.
latinIntro.cn: thigh 并非拉丁语词，拉丁语里表示同一部位的说法是 femur 与 coxa。

items.example: Theu is the earliest recorded form.
items.exampleCN: theu 是文献中最早的记录形式。

items.example: Thigh keeps the ancient sense almost unchanged.
items.exampleCN: thigh 几乎原封不动地保留了古老词义。

items.example: The suffix -s forms thighs.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -s 构成 thighs。

items.example: Bone combines with thigh in thigh bone.
items.exampleCN: bone 与 thigh 组合成 thigh bone。

items.example: High forms thigh-high for socks.
items.exampleCN: high 构成及大腿的长袜说法 thigh-high。

items.example: Muscle pairs with thigh in thigh muscles.
items.exampleCN: muscle 与 thigh 组成大腿肌肉的表达。

items.example: Femur is the Latin name for the thigh bone.
items.exampleCN: femur 是股骨的拉丁语名称。

items.example: Coxa is the Latin word for the hip.
items.exampleCN: coxa 是表示髋部的拉丁语词。

items.example: Crus gives words such as crural.
items.exampleCN: crus 衍生出 crural 一类词。

definition_zh: 多刺的；有刺的；棘手的；难办的
definition_en: full of thorns or sharp points, or (of a problem or issue) difficult and full of possible trouble
core_image: 枝上密布尖刺，手一伸进去就被扎得缩回
scene: 谈判桌上摆着最棘手的一项条款，谁开口都怕被刺到。The thorniest clause in the contract was left until the very end of the talks.
sceneCN: 这里 thorny 是「棘手的」（第 2 个义项：问题难缠、处处有坑）；句意：合同里最棘手的那条条款被留到谈判的最后才谈。

pos.zh: 棘手的；难办的；充满争议的

derivatives.zh: 基础名词，义为「刺；荆棘」；后缀 -y 表示「充满……的」，thorny 即长满刺的
thorny 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「多刺；棘手」
thorn 加否定后缀 -less 构成，义为「无刺的」
thorn 与 bush 复合而成，义为「荆棘丛」

senses.title: Full of thorns
senses.definition: covered with thorns or sharp spines that can prick you
senses.definitionCN: 长满刺或尖刺、伸手就会被扎到的
senses.example: We pushed through a thorny hedge to reach the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 我们穿过一道满是刺的树篱才到达大门。
senses.why: The adjective adds the very productive Old English suffix -y meaning full of to thorn, so the first sense is simply being full of thorns.
senses.whyCN: 形容词由名词 thorn 加古英语后缀 -y 构成，-y 表示「充满……的」，所以第一个义项就是字面的「长满刺」。

senses.title: Difficult and full of trouble
senses.definition: difficult to deal with because it is full of sensitive points or possible arguments
senses.definitionCN: 因为处处敏感、容易引发争论而难以处理的
senses.example: The committee must settle a thorny question of funding.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会必须解决一个棘手的经费问题。
senses.why: Touching a thorny plant hurts immediately, so a topic full of hidden traps is pictured as something that pricks whoever reaches into it.
senses.whyCN: 碰一下多刺的植物立刻会被扎痛，于是布满隐形陷阱的话题就被想成「谁伸手谁被扎」的东西，长出了「棘手」这一比喻义。

senses.title: A path full of thorns
senses.definition: used of a course, journey, or situation that is painful and filled with obstacles
senses.definitionCN: 形容一段行程或处境充满痛苦与阻碍的
senses.example: Their road to peace was long and thorny.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的和平之路漫长而布满荆棘。
senses.why: The literal hedgerow sense survives in the literary image of a path covered in thorns, a journey where every step cuts.
senses.whyCN: 字面义「满是刺的」在「荆棘之路」这类文学意象里被保留下来，形容每走一步都要被划伤的经历。

intro.en: Thorny is a native English compound of thorn and the adjective suffix -y, with a Germanic root behind both.
intro.cn: thorny 是英语本族词，由名词 thorn 加形容词后缀 -y 构成，两者都可上溯到日耳曼语。

items.en: A reconstructed form is usually written thurnuz, meaning a thorn or spine.
items.cn: 一般重构为 thurnuz，义为「刺、尖刺」。

items.en: Thorn is the ordinary noun for a spine or thorn bush.
items.cn: 古英语 thorn 指刺或带刺的灌木。

items.en: The suffix -y, from an older ending -ig, means full of or having the quality of.
items.cn: 后缀 -y 来自更早的 -ig，意为「充满……的、具有……性质的」。

items.en: Thorny appears in Middle English as the adjective of thorn.
items.cn: 中古英语时期 thorny 作为 thorn 的形容词形式出现。

items.en: Writers begin to apply the word to arguments and difficulties rather than plants.
items.cn: 这一时期的作者开始把该词用在争论与困难上，而不只用于植物。

items.en: Thorny is now most common in the figurative phrase a thorny issue.
items.cn: 现代英语中 thorny 最常见的用法是比喻性的搭配，指「棘手的问题」。

note.en: Thorny shares its stem with thorn and grows from the same prickly family as prickle and bristle.
note.cn: thorny 与 thorn 同根，与 prickle、bristle 同属「扎人」的词汇家族。

entries.definition: a sharp pointed part on a plant
the state of being thorny
having no thorns
covered with sharp points, or easily offended
having many sharp points
difficult to deal with or do

normalIntro.en: Thorny is built on thorn plus -y, so the meaning moves from a prickly plant to a prickly problem.
normalIntro.cn: thorny 由 thorn 加 -y 构成，意义从「刺人的植物」延伸到「刺手的问题」。

normal.en: Thorn is a sharp spine on a plant, and -y means full of.
normal.cn: thorn 是植物上的尖刺，-y 表示「充满」，合起来就是「多刺的」。

normal.en: Write the pair thorn and thorny, then compare it with health and healthy.
normal.cn: 把 thorn 与 thorny 成对记，再和 health 与 healthy 的构词比一比。

normal.en: A thorny issue is an issue nobody wants to touch because it stings.
normal.cn: 棘手的问题就像谁都不愿碰的刺，一碰就疼。

normal.en: The comparative is thornier with an i, so the y changes to i before the ending.
normal.cn: 比较级是 thornier，词尾的 y 先变 i 再加词尾。

normal.en: Thornless says no thorns, just as hopeless says no hope.
normal.cn: thornless 表示「无刺」，正如 hopeless 表示「无望」。

abstract.en: Picture a hedge so thick with spikes that the hedge is all that you see.
abstract.cn: 想象一道密密的带刺树篱，满眼只剩尖刺。

abstract.en: Imagine a folder labelled budget reform opening and a spike springing out.
abstract.cn: 想象打开一个写着预算改革的文件夹，里面弹出一根尖刺。

abstract.en: Think of a barefoot walk up a hill where every step hurts.
abstract.cn: 想象赤脚走上坡路，每一步都刺痛。

examples.en: They spent a long afternoon on the thorny question of fees.
examples.cn: 他们花了一个漫长的下午讨论棘手的收费问题。

examples.en: The path through the wood was narrow and thorny.
examples.cn: 穿过树林的小路又窄又满是荆棘。

examples.en: Rising costs made the next round of talks even thornier.
examples.cn: 成本上升让下一轮会谈变得更加棘手。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「索尼」牌随身听缠满了耳机线，像绕了一圈尖刺，越想理越棘手；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 thorn（刺）＋形容词后缀 -y（充满……的，源自古英语 -ig）→ thorny（多刺的）→ 比喻为「处处扎人的」，即棘手的。

sensesIntro.en: Thorny starts as the plain adjective of thorn, extends to anything covered with spines, and then refers to problems, paths, or situations that hurt those who touch them.
sensesIntro.cn: thorny 先是 thorn 的普通形容词，指「长满刺」；再泛指布满尖刺之物；最后指让人一碰就吃亏的问题、道路或处境。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bush crowded with sharp spines
core.cn: 核心意象：一丛密布尖刺的灌木。

branches.en: The literal reading grows straight from thorn plus the suffix -y.
branches.cn: 字面义直接由 thorn 加后缀 -y 生长而来。

branches.en: A problem that pricks whoever touches it is the dominant modern sense.
branches.cn: 「谁碰谁被扎」的问题，是现代最常见的义项。

branches.en: The thorny path keeps the hedge image in a literary register.
branches.cn: 「荆棘之路」以文学语体保留了树篱的意象。

branches.en: Both a real thorn and a thorny road depend on the physical picture of spines.
branches.cn: 真实的刺与荆棘之路都依赖「尖刺在眼前」的画面。

branches.en: A road full of thorns and a thorny issue both describe difficulty that hurts.
branches.cn: 布满荆棘的路与棘手的问题都形容「会让人吃亏」的困难。

intro.en: Thorny is a real morphology lesson: a free root thorn and the suffix -y, with relatives such as thornless and thorniness.
intro.cn: thorny 是构词法的好例子：自由词根 thorn 加后缀 -y，还有 thornless、thorniness 等同族词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor here, since thorn and -y are both Germanic and the forms listed are English words.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语来源，thorn 与 -y 都是日耳曼语成分，下面列出的都是英语同族词。

items.meaning: a sharp spine on a plant
items.example: A thorn caught on her sleeve.
items.exampleCN: 一根刺钩住了她的袖子。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of
items.example: The suffix -y turns thorn into thorny.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 把 thorn 变成 thorny。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ness forms thorniness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 thorniness。

items.example: The suffix -less forms thornless.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -less 构成 thornless。

items.example: Thornbush joins thorn and bush.
items.exampleCN: thornbush 由 thorn 与 bush 合成。

items.example: Thorny keeps both the plant sense and the metaphor.
items.exampleCN: thorny 兼有植物义与比喻义。

items.meaning: a small sharp point on a plant or animal
items.example: Prickle belongs to the same sting vocabulary.
items.exampleCN: prickle 属于同一个「扎人」词汇群。

items.meaning: to hurt with a sharp pain
items.example: Sting supplies the pain behind the metaphor.
items.exampleCN: sting 提供了比喻义里的「刺痛感」。

items.example: A hedge is often the scene of thorny plants.
items.exampleCN: 树篱常是带刺植物生长的场景。

definition_zh: 门槛；起点；开端；临界值；阈值
definition_en: the strip at the bottom of a doorway, or the point at which something begins, changes, or takes effect
core_image: 脚下的那道横木，迈过去就进了门
scene: 只要收入过了一条线，家庭就能申请这档补贴。A family can claim this benefit once its income passes the threshold set by the government.
sceneCN: 这里 threshold 是「临界线、起算点」（第 3 个义项：使某事生效的界限）；句意：家庭收入一旦超过政府设定的门槛线，就可以申领这项补贴。

pos.zh: 临界值；阈值；门槛（生效的界限）

derivatives.zh: threshold 加 -ing 构成的技术名词，指在图像处理或信号处理中「取阈值」
threshold 加 -ed 构成，技术语境中指「已按阈值处理过的」
threshold 加 -less 构成，指「无阈值的、不设门槛的」

senses.title: The strip at the bottom of a door
senses.definition: the piece of wood or stone at the bottom of a doorway that you step over
senses.definitionCN: 门口地面上供人跨过的那块木头或石头
senses.example: She wiped her shoes on the threshold before going in.
senses.exampleCN: 她进门前在门槛上蹭了蹭鞋。
senses.why: The oldest sense names the physical beam you step across, and every later sense is a picture of passing from one side to the other.
senses.whyCN: 最早的义项就是脚下跨过的那根横木，之后所有义项都借用了「从一边跨到另一边」的画面。

senses.title: The beginning of something new
senses.definition: the point at which a new period, state, or stage begins
senses.definitionCN: 新阶段、新状况开始的那个时点
senses.example: The country stands on the threshold of a new era.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家正处在新时代的门槛上。
senses.why: Standing in a doorway means you are about to enter, so the threshold came to mean the very beginning of something.
senses.whyCN: 站在门口就意味着马上要进去，所以门槛被用来表示某事「刚开始」的那一刻。

senses.title: A limit that triggers change
senses.definition: the level or amount at which something starts to happen or take effect
senses.definitionCN: 某事开始发生或开始生效的那个水平或数量
senses.example: Anyone earning above the threshold must pay the higher rate.
senses.exampleCN: 收入超过该门槛的人都必须按更高的税率缴税。
senses.why: In science and law the crossing image becomes exact: below the line nothing happens, above it the effect begins.
senses.whyCN: 在科学和法律里，「跨过」的图像被精确化：线下一律不触发，线上效果才开始。

senses.title: The point where a sensation becomes felt
senses.definition: the weakest stimulus that can be noticed, or the point past which pain or stress can be felt
senses.definitionCN: 能被察觉的最弱刺激，或疼痛、压力开始被感受到的界限
senses.example: His pain threshold is unusually high.
senses.exampleCN: 他的痛阈异常高。
senses.why: A perfectly straight extension of the limit sense: the body and mind have their own doorways, and below them nothing is registered.
senses.whyCN: 这是「界限」义的直接延伸：身体和心理也有自己的门槛，低于门槛就感受不到。

senses.title: A fixed level in analysis
senses.definition: a fixed value used in computing an image or a signal that decides what is kept and what is dropped
senses.definitionCN: 处理图像或信号时用来决定保留与舍弃的固定数值
senses.example: The program keeps every pixel brighter than the threshold.
senses.exampleCN: 这个程序保留所有亮度高于阈值的像素。
senses.why: Engineering turns the doorway into a number, and things above that number pass through while the rest are stopped.
senses.whyCN: 工程技术把「门」变成数字，高于这个数的通过，其余被挡在门外。

intro.en: Threshold is a Germanic compound whose first element may be thresh, to stamp or tread, and the second element, sill or boards, is debated.
intro.cn: threshold 是日耳曼语复合词，第一部分可能来自 thresh（踩、踏），第二部分一般认为与 sill（门坎）或 boards 相关，学界尚有争论。

items.en: The word is recorded as therscold, threscold, and threschwold, with several spelling variants.
items.cn: 古英语中出现 therscold、threscold、threschwold 等多种拼写变体。

items.en: The first element is usually connected with threscan, to thresh or tread out grain.
items.cn: 第一部分一般认为与 threscan（打谷、用脚踩）有关。

items.en: Scholars debate whether the second element is sill, boards, or a reconstructed word for stepping place.
items.cn: 第二部分的来源学界有争论：一说与 sill（门坎）有关，一说与 boards（木板）有关，还有人认为是重构的「踩踏之处」。

items.en: Middle English threschold keeps the concrete sense of the beam at the foot of a door.
items.cn: 中古英语 threschold 保留「门下横木」的具体含义。

items.en: The word develops the figures of entering and beginning, followed by scientific limits.
items.cn: 此后该词发展出「进入」「开端」的比喻义，并进一步获得科学上「界限」的含义。

items.en: Psychologists and engineers adopt it for the value at which a stimulus or a change begins to register.
items.cn: 现代英语中心理学家和工程师用它指「刺激或变化开始被记录的那个数值」。

note.en: Threshold sits with doorway and sill in the house vocabulary, and with limits such as limit and boundary in meaning.
note.cn: threshold 与 doorway、sill 同属「房屋与门口」的词汇场，在意义上则与 limit、boundary 这些「界限」词相邻。

entries.definition: to beat grain to separate it from the husks
entries.definitionCN: 打谷；脱粒（一般认为与本词第一部分有关）

entries.definition: the flat piece at the bottom of a door or window
entries.definitionCN: 门槛；窗台（与第二部分来源相关）

entries.definition: the opening through which you enter a room
entries.definitionCN: 门口；门洞（只是场景相近，并非同源）

entries.definition: the greatest amount that is allowed
a line that marks the edge of something
the very edge of something, especially something dangerous

normalIntro.en: Threshold can be split into thresh, to stamp, and an old word for the sill under a door, so the whole word means the treadboard.
normalIntro.cn: threshold 可拆成 thresh（踩、踏）与表示门下横木的古词，整词就是「踩踏用的横木」。

normal.en: Link threshold with thresh, to tread or stamp grain, and the sense of treading under a door.
normal.cn: 把 threshold 与 thresh（踩、打谷）联系起来，记住「在门下踩过」的画面。

normal.en: The phrase on the threshold of means just about to begin.
normal.cn: 短语 on the threshold of 表示「即将开始、处在……的前夕」。

normal.en: Cross the threshold literally means stepping in, and figuratively means entering a new stage.
normal.cn: cross the threshold 字面是跨过门槛，引申为进入新阶段。

normal.en: In science the word means a number at which an effect starts, as in the pain threshold.
normal.cn: 在科学语境里它指效果开始发生的数值，如痛阈。

normal.en: Compare threshold with the habit word on the doorstep, both about the entry to a home.
normal.cn: 可以把 threshold 与表示门前台阶的 doorstep 对比，两者都与家门口有关。

abstract.en: Picture a worn wooden beam and one foot lifting over it.
abstract.cn: 想象一根被磨旧的木门槛，一只脚正抬起来跨过去。

abstract.en: Imagine a thermometer whose red line reaches a marked level and the alarm rings.
abstract.cn: 想象温度计的红色液柱升到标记线，警报随之响起。

abstract.en: Think of a door that is silent until someone turns the handle just enough.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇无声的门，把手转到刚好够的角度才会开启。

examples.en: Grandmother stood at the threshold and waved us off.
examples.cn: 祖母站在门槛上挥手送我们离开。

examples.en: The delay pushed the project to the threshold of failure.
examples.cn: 这次延误把项目推到了失败的边缘。

examples.en: Raising the threshold for free shipping would cut costs.
examples.cn: 提高包邮的门槛可以降低成本。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死雷守」——站在门上死死守着那道门槛，不让可疑的人跨过去；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 therscold／threscold：第一部分一般认为与 threscan（踩、打谷）相关，第二部分来源存疑（一说 sill「门坎」，一说 boards「木板」）→ threshold（门槛）→ 开端 → 临界阈值。

sensesIntro.en: Threshold begins with the beam you cross at a door and fans out into the start of an era, a legal or scientific limit, the limit of sensation, and a fixed value in computing.
sensesIntro.cn: threshold 先从跨过的门下横木出发，扩展到时代的开端、法律与科学的界限、感觉的界限，以及计算中的固定阈值。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a beam under a door with one foot lifting over it
core.cn: 核心意象：门槛横木，一只脚正要跨过去。

branches.en: The physical beam under a doorway is the source of every other sense.
branches.cn: 门下那根实体横木是所有其他义项的源头。

branches.en: Being about to enter turns into the idea of a fresh start.
branches.cn: 「正要进门」转化为「全新的开始」。

branches.en: The crossing line becomes the level at which something starts to happen.
branches.cn: 跨越的那条线变成「事情开始发生」的水平。

branches.en: Sensation and computation each borrow the doorway as a precise value.
branches.cn: 感觉与计算各自把「门」借用为精确数值。

branches.en: A beginning and a trigger value share the same picture of passing from one state to another.
branches.cn: 开端与触发值共享「从一个状态跨到另一个状态」的画面。

intro.en: Threshold is a compound, not a word built with living prefixes or suffixes, so its parts are older elements such as the stem thresh and the second part.
intro.cn: threshold 是复合词，不是由现代词缀构成的，它的部件是更古老的部分：前段 thresh 与后段。

latinIntro.en: No Latin ancestor is involved, and the related forms here are native English words and parts.
latinIntro.cn: 该词没有拉丁语来源，下面列出的都是英语本族词或构词成分。

items.meaning: to beat grain or to tread
items.example: Thresh shares its stem with the first part of threshold.
items.exampleCN: thresh 与 threshold 的前半段同词干。

items.meaning: the flat base of a door or window
items.example: Sill names a similar object at the foot of a door.
items.exampleCN: sill 指门口处类似的一块底梁。

items.meaning: a door beam or a limit
items.example: Threshold keeps both the house sense and the limit sense.
items.exampleCN: threshold 兼有「家的门」与「界限」两层含义。

items.example: The doorway frames the threshold you cross.
items.exampleCN: 门洞框住了要跨过的门槛。

items.example: The suffix -less forms thresholdless.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -less 构成 thresholdless。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或过程的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ing forms thresholding.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 thresholding。

items.example: Thresholds follow the regular -s plural.
items.exampleCN: thresholds 遵循常规的 -s 复数规则。

items.meaning: the Latin word for a threshold, used in psychology
items.meaningCN: 拉丁语中表示「门槛」的词，心理学借来指「阈限」
items.example: The limen and the threshold name the same line.
items.exampleCN: limen 与 threshold 命名的是同一条界线。

latinEntries.meaning: belonging to a boundary or beginning stage
latinEntries.meaningCN: 属于界限或过渡阶段的
